💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that space is known as the final frontier.
  • With the rise of satellite services, defense capabilities, and even the proposed future of space-based data centers, companies are moving swiftly to capture the economic opportunity in orbit and beyond, with potentially trillions of dollars in value to be created in the decades ahead.
  • Three hot stocks of various sizes trying to win in the space economy are Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.78%) (SpaceX for short), Rocket Lab (RKLB -1.17%), and Planet Labs (PL -0.71%).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that space is known as the final frontier. It might be the final area to drive global economic growth.

With the rise of satellite services, defense capabilities, and even the proposed future of space-based data centers, companies are moving swiftly to capture the economic opportunity in orbit and beyond, with potentially trillions of dollars in value to be created in the decades ahead.

Three hot stocks of various sizes trying to win in the space economy are Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.78%) (SpaceX for short), Rocket Lab (RKLB -1.17%), and Planet Labs (PL -0.71%). Here's what a $1,000 investment in each could be worth by 2030, and how risky the stocks are today.

Sources indicate that elon Musk's rocket company -- and one that's becoming more focused on artificial intelligence (AI) -- holds a dominant position in the large-rocket launch segment, giving it immense power to decide what gets into orbit. Increasingly, it has prioritized launching its own satellites into orbit for the Starlink internet service. Revenue from this segment grew nearly 70% year over year last quarter to $5.2 billion, and it is growing like a weed worldwide.

Long term, SpaceX is trying aggressively to become a large player in the AI infrastructure market. It is spending close to the same levels as the hyperscalers on building data centers and saw its AI revenue jump by around 10 times to $7.56 billion last quarter. Musk projects annualized revenue will grow at a tremendous pace next year, reaching $500 billion by the fourth quarter of 2027.

It will be a tall task, but to reach its current market cap of $1.9 trillion and generate gains for shareholders through 2030, a scenario like this needs to unfold.

The one tech giant with a chance to match SpaceX's capabilities is Rocket Lab, which has demonstrated a consistent ability to launch commercial payloads for customers far better than any other competitor to Musk's company.

Its small Electron rocket is closing in on 100 releases, driving revenue to $53 million last quarter, up from $41 million a year prior. Like SpaceX, Rocket Lab is building its own medium-lift vehicle to drive more revenue per launch. Its name is Neutron, and it could earn upward of $70 million per launch, which is more than Rocket Lab now generates from its business in a quarter.

NASDAQ · As of 9:52 AM ET 11/17/26.

And like SpaceX, it is investing in its own satellite development and has acquired satellite communications company Iridium, which still needs regulatory approvals before the merger is completed. There is a ton of potential for Rocket Lab if it can put all its projects together and become the second fully integrated launch provider alongside SpaceX. With a market cap of $40 billion and trailing-12-month revenue below $1 billion, a lot will need to go right in order for this stock to deliver good returns for anyone investing today.

A company not in the launch business, but one that benefits from the growth of commercial payload capacity, is Planet Labs.

It has a niche offering building a constellation of imaging satellites that can monitor developments across the globe from low Earth orbit. This is useful for environmental, commercial, and military activities, which is why it is signing huge contracts around the globe.

NYSE · As of 9:52 AM ET 11/17/26.

Last quarter, revenue jumped 58% year over year to $116 million, with its backlog growing as well. As with the other two stocks on this list, this level of growth will need to continue for Planet Labs to justify its current valuation, with a market cap of $5.22 billion.

Overall, these are three high-risk stocks growing north of 50% year over year, but at steep valuations. A $1,000 investment in each could deliver multibagger returns, reaching $10,000 in combined gains by 2030, but only if everything goes right.

Recent findings suggest that generally, in business and investing, the perfect future does not materialize. For that reason, it will pay to maintain some skepticism about how these stocks will perform, despite the space economy's huge potential, since these valuations have gotten well ahead of underlying business fundamentals.

Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1132 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the world of Linux, distro hopping is practically a spectator sport.
  • Industry observers note that also: Ubuntu 26.04 vs.
  • However, for those new to Linux, the idea of leaving behind a distribution that’s been working just fine can be daunting, especially when you’re considering jumping to a distribution that isn’t as familiar and uses different technology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the world of Linux, distro hopping is practically a spectator sport. At some point, we get bored with the distro we’re using and decide to try something fresh. Perhaps there’s a distro that offers better features, works with more hardware, or has a larger support community. There are so many reasons for switching distros.

Industry observers note that also: Ubuntu 26.04 vs. Fedora 44: My verdict.

However, for those new to Linux, the idea of leaving behind a distribution that’s been working just fine can be daunting, especially when you’re considering jumping to a distribution that isn’t as familiar and uses different technology.

It has been revealed that as a upcoming Linux user decades ago, I started with Caldera Open Linux 1.0 and immediately jumped to Red Hat Linux 5.2 (before Red Hat became Fedora). I stayed with Red Hat for years, until I found Ubuntu (I believe it was version 4).

Back then, making the jump wasn’t nearly as easy as it is now; in fact, it was unnerving. I was so used to how Fedora did things that I wasn’t certain I’d be able to acclimate.

In a recent development, but I did! And then, after realizing that hopping from one distro to another wasn’t the end of the world, I hopped around for a few years, from distro to distro until I settled back on Ubuntu-based distributions.

Industry observers note that also: Done with Debian Linux distros? Try Fedora next.

It has been revealed that it’s a lot, but it doesn’t have to be nearly as daunting as it seems. In fact, it can be exciting and fun. If you’re considering a jump from Ubuntu to Fedora, let me try to ease your concerns.

Industry observers note that first, let’s get the obvious out of the way: Ubuntu and Fedora are both Linux. It’s not like you’re jumping from Windows or MacOS to Linux. This is a lateral move, which is not nearly as fear-inducing.

Beyond that, Ubuntu and Fedora are much more similar than you might expect. They both have GUI tools for everything you need; they’re both secure; they both have great package managers and package manager front-ends; they both make it easy to install all of the software you need (and all of the software you need is readily available); and they’re both user-friendly.

Also: 5 of my favorite Linux distros for AI – and why.

If you get beyond the GUI and dip your toes into the command line, they both (mostly) use the same commands. Yes, there are some variations, but when you’re first learning the CLI (if you ever do — it’s not necessary), you’ll find those basic commands on Ubuntu are exactly the same as they are on Fedora.

Recent findings suggest that if you migrated from Windows to Ubuntu, you’ve already experienced what a faster operating system feels like. If you jump from Ubuntu to Fedora, you’re going to experience that again, because Fedora is (somewhat) faster than Ubuntu. The difference might not be as exaggerated as it was when you went from Windows to Linux, but it is noticeable. Animations are faster, apps open faster, and switching between desktops is faster — nearly every aspect of Fedora is a bit faster than in Ubuntu.

Also: Fedora 44 made me forget I was using Linux – in the best way.

I’ve tested several aspects with regard to the speed of Ubuntu and Fedora, and here are my conclusions:.

This is almost a tie. When rebooting from a logged-in desktop to the login screen, Fedora took 13.69 seconds, while Ubuntu took 14.31 seconds. The only caveat to that is if Fedora has updates that require a reboot, in which case Fedora takes considerably longer. The only time you have to reboot Ubuntu after an update is if the kernel is upgraded.

It has been revealed that fedora wins this one, especially when it comes to Flatpak and Snap apps. Snap apps simply cannot compete with the speed of Flatpak apps (more on this in a bit). I tested this by opening a Snap app on Ubuntu and a Flatpak app on Fedora, using GIMP (since I know GIMP takes a while to start). On Fedora, the Flatpak GIMP took 3.48 seconds, and on Ubuntu the Snap app version of GIMP took 4.34 seconds.

This is one area where Ubuntu has a slight edge, but only when installing via the default package manager (rather than Flatpak or Snap). I tested this by timing the installation of Audacity using each package manager (DNF5 and APT) from the command line. DNF5 installed Audacity in 15.34 seconds, whereas the Ubuntu installation took 14.61 seconds.

It has been revealed that generally speaking, Fedora not only ships with newer apps than Ubuntu, but it also gets updates faster than Ubuntu. That’s not to say that Ubuntu uses out-of-date packages; rather, Fedora is more cutting-edge than Ubuntu.

Also: 5 premium Linux distros absolutely worth paying for.

At the same time, that doesn’t mean Fedora uses unstable applications. All software that ships and/or is updated on Fedora is well-tested and stable — it’s just fresher.

Flatpaks and Snaps are universal package managers. Fedora ships with Flatpak, and Ubuntu is all-in on Snaps. While these two technologies have the same goal (making software installation easier and more secure), they take different approaches.

In a recent development, first off, Flatpak was created by Red Hat, while Snap was created by Canonical. Snap is partially proprietary, while Flatpak is fully open-source. Flatpak enforces mandatory sandboxing, whereas Snap makes sandboxing optional. Flatpak apps launch faster than Snap apps. Finally, Snap packages are automatically updated, whereas Flatpak apps require manual updates.

Also: My favorite GNOME-based Linux distros.

Overall, Flatpak is widely considered the superior technology by the Linux community.

In my experience, Flatpak is a better technology for the desktop, whereas Snap is best suited for servers.

Recent findings suggest that if you were to look at both Ubuntu and Fedora, you would swear they use different desktop environments. Au contraire, mon ami. Both Fedora and Ubuntu use GNOME; the difference is that Ubuntu customizes GNOME to look more like the Ubuntu Unity UI Canonical tested back in 2010. Since then, Ubuntu adopted GNOME and customized it so it wouldn’t irk customers who had grown accustomed to Unity.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

Fedora, on the other hand, sticks with a stock installation of GNOME for its flagship release. The good news is that, if you like the Ubuntu take on GNOME, you can install the necessary GNOME extensions (the main one being Dash to Panel) to get a similar layout. You can also get the Unity-like top bar by installing the Unite-Shell extension.

Ray Dalio says Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
  • In a recent development, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
  • "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

In a recent development, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

"I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

It has been revealed that the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio said. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

Bessent noted in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

Industry observers note that after years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

To solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

First, Dalio stated the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

It has been revealed that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio noted. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

Sources indicate that dalio stated it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

Industry observers note that dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder remarked.

According to recent reports, dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since OpenAI debuted ChatGPT to the public in late November 2022, the stock market has enjoyed a pretty epic rally fueled by enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence (AI).
  • In a recent development, the AI revolution has propelled stock market valuations to historically elevated levels, raising concerns that investors may be witnessing another bubble.
  • It has been revealed that developed by economist Robert Shiller, the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio compares the S&P 500's price with its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the last 10 years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since OpenAI debuted ChatGPT to the public in late November 2022, the stock market has enjoyed a pretty epic rally fueled by enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence (AI). Over the last four years, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.04%) has gained 85%, while the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +0.01%) has surged 119%. Even the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -0.35%) has advanced by 51%, illustrating how the bull market has extended beyond technology stocks.

In a recent development, the AI revolution has propelled stock market valuations to historically elevated levels, raising concerns that investors may be witnessing another bubble. One useful valuation tool suggests investors have good reason to be cautious right now, although its history also demonstrates why attempting to time the market is often a costly mistake.

It has been revealed that developed by economist Robert Shiller, the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio compares the S&P 500's price with its average inflation-adjusted earnings over the last 10 years. Unlike the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which measures a company using one year of historical or projected profits, the CAPE ratio smooths out fluctuations in earnings across economic cycles. This makes it useful for evaluating whether the broader stock market is expensive or reasonably valued relative to historical levels.

Recent findings suggest that historically, the CAPE ratio has averaged approximately 18. However, recent readings have sustained above 40. Such elevated valuations can make stocks vulnerable to disappointing earnings, rising interest rates, or shifts in investor sentiment.

Shiller CAPE Ratio data by YCharts.

An elevated CAPE ratio doesn't automatically mean a stock market crash is imminent. To understand why investors shouldn't use the CAPE ratio as a market-timing tool, it's worth examining three historical periods when valuations approached or exceeded 40.

Sources indicate that these three episodes illustrate why the CAPE ratio is more useful for assessing long-term investment risk than predicting short-term market fluctuations. Investors who sold simply because valuations became historically expensive in early 1999 would have actually missed additional gains before the dot-com bubble eventually burst. Similarly, today's elevated valuations don't necessarily establish when the next downturn will inevitably begin or how severe it could become.

Although the historical evidence suggests the market could be headed for disappointing returns, it also offers an encouraging lesson for investors with a long-term time horizon.

Consider someone who invested $10,000 in an S&P 500 index fund on March 24, 2000, right before the dot-com collapse. Despite experiencing multiple bear markets and recessions over the following decades, that investment would have grown to approximately $68,400 by Nov. 13.

Industry observers note that someone who invested $10,000 at the S&P 500's peak on Jan. 3, 2022 would have first endured a 25% decline over the following nine months. However, the investment would eventually have recovered and grown to about $15,800 if they had held through today.

Although the CAPE ratio has approached or exceeded 40 during periods of stock market euphoria, it has never reliably provided a timetable for the next correction or bear market. Investors who maintain diversified portfolios, avoid chasing momentum, and remain invested through volatility over the long term have always benefited from the stock market's resiliency.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic often refers to its Claude agent as your coworker. Soon, the company noted, it will be able to join your meetings like one, and start working on the tasks you and your team are discussing live.

Also: I locked down my OpenClaw agent with Claude Code – then dared it to escape.

“Claude Meetings will let you add Claude to a call to take notes and upgrade the documents your team is working on during the conversation,” Anthropic noted. The feature, which will be available for Team and Enterprise looks, theoretically goes beyond something like Gemini’s Google Meet transcription and note-taking, which identifies action items but doesn’t proactively contribute to them.

Recent findings suggest that in material shared with ZDNET prior to the launch, the organization mentioned Claude “won’t join a call with outside guests unless an admin allows it, and it leaves if one joins anyway.” The company also said Claude Meetings will be on by default for Team plans, but Enterprise admins will be able to choose who gets it. The feature won’t work for organizations with “zero data retention (ZDR), HIPAA-ready configuration or customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).”.

The tech giant did not clarify when Meetings would roll out, but unveiled several other updates for companies that are available now.

To further keep as much of your work ecosystem within the Claude universe, Anthropic released a new Whiteboards feature in beta.

Also: Claude’s Record-a-Skill cut my research to minutes.

“Now, you can talk through a messy plan out loud with Claude, and Claude can turn it into a board with a timeline with owners and dates, so you and your team can collaborate in real time,” Anthropic said. Claude will group crowdsourced notes into themes and action items. Maybe double-check the results of that spew before locking anything in.

After brain-dumping like you might on a physical whiteboard, Anthropic remarked, Claude can turn that output into a deck or document, or export it to other tools for next steps.

Sources indicate that A new Sheets feature is exactly as it sounds: Claude can now create shareable spreadsheets from a prompt and edit inside cells with trackable changes. But it’s not fully replacing the old guard of spreadsheets just yet.

Recent findings suggest that “When you need the full functionality of Excel, you can export your file to .xlsx or CSV, or use Claude for Excel,” Anthropic noted. “You can also continue working in partner tools including Airtable, Asana, monday.com, and Smartsheet.”.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a free, local AI stack.

Claude Dashboards, which only launched in beta last month, is now called Data. The tool can query manufacturer data from large external services such as Amazon Redshift and ClickHouse and comes with tracked changes and faster loading thanks to caching. According to Anthropic, it’s intended to let companies standardize metrics to avoid having conflicting data, surface data stories, and create a live source of truth everyone can access.

Sources indicate that “With live sharing, your colleagues can see up-to-date numbers when they open a shared dashboard, even if they don’t have access to the connectors that keep that data current. Viewers see the results of the queries you’ve approved, and can’t run others with your access,” the company said.

Anthropic remarked that for Team aims, all three features are on by default. For Enterprise plans, only Claude Data will be on by default starting Nov. 19. Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default, though you can adjust those settings in Artifacts.

Anthropic has maintained a lead over OpenAI by focusing on enterprise clients first, while OpenAI has prioritized several consumer products. Releases like this are unsurprising, as they serve Anthropic’s primary base. Both Anthropic and OpenAI are increasingly branching into workplace and productivity software for large-scale companies. That stated, Anthropic’s recent release of a personal finance tool rivals OpenAI’s existing equivalent geared toward consumers.

Also: Claude’s newly introduced Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending.

Industry observers note that in September, at its Dev Day, OpenAI released ChatGPT Space, which houses document and slide creation tools reminiscent of Google Workspace. Before that, Anthropic had similarly consolidated its document and slide creation features into a single hub.

Industry observers note that if there’s a slight differentiator here versus Google Workspace, it’s interface seamlessness. Anthropic has designed Claude itself as the starting point for a range of workplace deliverables, rather than maintaining distinct applications that can promptly feel siloed.

Apple Rolls out Latest App to Study How People Use AI for Health

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Since 2019, when Apple first launched its Research app, the company has partnered with medical universities and institutions to run a range of health studies on hearing, heart health and movement, women’s health and, most recently, the Apple Health Study, which covers a wide variety of health areas.
  • On Sunday, Apple debuted its latest study, and it comes with its own app: the Apple Health AI Study.
  • During a press briefing, Apple said the study aims to understand how people interact with conversational health AI tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2019, when Apple first launched its Research app, the company has partnered with medical universities and institutions to run a range of health studies on hearing, heart health and movement, women’s health and, most recently, the Apple Health Study, which covers a wide variety of health areas.

On Sunday, Apple debuted its latest study, and it comes with its own app: the Apple Health AI Study.

During a press briefing, Apple said the study aims to understand how people interact with conversational health AI tools. To do so, it will examine comprehension, response quality, the drivers of user trust and everyday health actions.

The goal? To inform the responsible design of health AI experiences for both Apple and the industry and to explore how health AI might help people prepare for doctor’s visits. Key questions the study aims to address include: Do users understand the information provided by health AI? Do they trust it? Is it helpful?

This is particularly relevant considering that one in three US adults use AI chatbots for health information.

Study data will not be used to train AI models, but it may inform Apple’s feature development.

To facilitate the study, Apple is partnering with OpenEvidence, an AI platform designed specifically for doctors. It generates answers using medical information from these partners: The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, National Comprehensive Cancer Network, Nature and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews.

In the dedicated app, study participants can ask the AI their text-based health questions and then see answers with linked, peer-reviewed clinical citations. They can also choose to share their HealthKit data, including sleep, lab results, activity and resting heart rate, for more personalized answers.

HealthKit is Apple’s hub for health and fitness data collected on the iPhone and Apple Watch.

The Apple Health AI Usage Study is open to 200,000 participants. You must be in the US and age 21 or older to participate. An Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) running iOS 26 or later is also required.

It has been revealed that why an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone? According to Apple, the study app requires the processing capabilities of those iPhones, and it uses on-device Apple Foundation Models that are part of Apple Intelligence. These models provide access to any large language model. For example, as part of the study, these models are used to classify question categories.

Industry observers note that each participant is asked to participate for up to 12 months. During this time, they can ask questions about general health, specific symptoms, recovery from a procedure and their own uploaded health data, as examples.

In addition to a baseline survey, participants will receive monthly surveys and additional surveys specific to preparing for doctor’s visits.

Participants will also be prompted to check in with the app. For instance, if you have a paired Apple Watch, you will receive notifications to check in, along with suggested topics to explore.

If there is a complete lack of participation, a participant may potentially be removed from the study.

In a recent development, after downloading the Apple Health AI Study app, participants must complete a mandatory onboarding process that includes informed consent. They will also be asked to share their demographic information, such as race, age and education level, which will be used to explore how these factors may affect their preferences and communication needs. Then, they can start asking the AI questions.

The iPhone first processes questions using tools designed to remove details that could identify participants. They then go to a secure cloud-based study environment managed by a third-party study support contractor called UST Global, where queries are delinked from individual participant IDs and screened using tools designed to further remove any remaining personal details. Lastly, this info is sent to OpenEvidence, where answers are generated using supporting reference materials.

OpenEvidence will delete both question and response data within 24 hours.

A small group of Apple researchers will have access to coded versions of survey responses, separated from personally identifiable information, summaries of conversations and categories of the most common conversation types.

Within the study app, there are also safety guardrails that detect concerning questions and respond by suggesting that a participant follow up with a provider or other resources if needed.

There is no live monitoring, and study staff won’t contact participants if any questions related to self-harm are asked.

It’s also up to the participant whether they share any HealthKit metrics. They will first have to choose to upload their clinical health records to Apple’s Health app, and then separately choose to share those records from the Health app to the new Apple Health AI Study app.

According to recent reports, the Apple Health AI Study app is now available in the App Store. As of now, there is no set publication date for the study.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gemini Intelligence is spreading beyond the Google Pixel 11 lineup to the Pixel 10, the upcoming Motorola Signature 27, and several of Samsung’s Galaxy foldables and flagship phones.

Though Google often offers its most upgraded features to other Android phone manufacturers, there are some features that are Pixel-exclusive or come to Pixel users first. This time, Gemini Intelligence is coming to Android Auto, but only for eligible Pixel users.

Also: I’m an Android Auto ride or die – but Apple CarPlay beats it on these 3 features.

Google’s blog post states that Pixel people with Gemini Intelligence can expect it to gather information from their apps and surface it to their car’s infotainment screen. Google’s example is that if a friend texts you asking where you’re meeting for Pilates, Gemini Intelligence can find the correct confirmation email and offer to send it with one tap.

To access Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto, the Gemini app and subsequent setup are required; it’s available in select countries to users aged 18 and older, and feature availability will vary.

With more context about your messages, emails, and calendar events, a more capable assistant can complete cross-app tasks while driving, such as “remind me to buy mom a birthday card before her birthday” or “which route to my dentist appointment will be the fastest?” I often use Siri AI in CarPlay for tasks like these, and Gemini operates the same way. However, these tasks require user input first; what makes an AI assistant in in-car software great is when it suggests tasks before you ask for them.

In a recent development, siri suggests to me when I should leave my house for an upcoming event in my calendar, such as a dinner reservation, flight, or doctor’s appointment, based on traffic conditions. It looks like Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto will offer the same assistance. I’ve reached out to Google to confirm, and will patch this article if I get a response.

Also: 4 wireless Android Auto adapters we recommend (and they’re cheap).

I find Siri’s upgraded capabilities most useful when I have a busy day and heavy Atlanta traffic is thrown in the mix. Sometimes people need information about where to meet up, but I don’t remember the exact name of the location or which street it’s on. It’s difficult to search through my old messages or emails while staying alert to crazed drivers on the interstate, so a smarter AI assistant comes in handy.

It has been revealed that though Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto is reserved for Pixel consumers, the upgrade follows a series of improvements Google has rolled out to its in-car software. Non-Pixel Android phones and Android phones without Gemini Intelligence can use Personal Intelligence, which connects Gemini across your Google Maps, Photos, or Gmail data.

Industry observers note that personal Intelligence customers can ask Gemini to navigate to a restaurant with a specific cuisine or vibe, or search their photos to find a car wash they photographed last week. Gemini Intelligence is more proactive and expansive, drawing on more sensitive data from your phone, such as messages, while Personal Intelligence relies solely on data from your Google services.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investors weighing growth in snacks against the stability of hygiene products must decide whether Hershey (HSY -0.85%) or Kimberly-Clark (KMB -0.95%) offers the most compelling path forward for a diversified portfolio.

Industry observers note that while Hershey is defined by its dominance in the chocolate and snack markets, Kimberly-Clark focuses on essential personal care and tissue products. These businesses are often compared because they both provide products that consumers tend to buy regardless of economic conditions, making them staples for many long-term investment portfolios.

In a recent development, hershey sells chocolate, sweets, and mints in more than 65 countries under more than 85 brand names. Its core strength lies in North American confectionery and salty snacks through iconic brands like Hershey's and Reese's. In its latest annual report, the company identified McLane Company, Inc. as its largest customer, representing nearly 27% of net sales. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as this single distributor serves as the primary gateway to large retailers like Walmart Inc.

Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each company's latest full fiscal year. For the fiscal year ended in 2025, Hershey generated revenue of nearly $11.7 billion, representing roughly 4.4% growth over the prior year. Despite the top-line increase, the company reported net income of approximately $883.3 million, down from the $2.2 billion earned in fiscal 2024.

Industry observers note that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the tech giant maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 1.2x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, helping investors understand how much a firm relies on borrowed money. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities to assess liquidity, is roughly 1.2x. During the same period, Hershey generated free cash flow of nearly $1.7 billion, representing the cash remaining after the business covers its operating expenses and capital investments.

Kimberly-Clark operates in the consumer staples stocks arena, focusing on essential fiber-based and nonwoven products. Its portfolio includes household staples such as Huggies and Kleenex, with about half of its net sales coming from markets outside the U.S. Its largest customer is Walmart Inc., which accounted for nearly 16% of net sales in its most recent fiscal year. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as a significant portion of volume relies on one retail partner.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, the company reported revenue of close to $16.4 billion. This represented a revenue decrease of roughly 2.1% compared to the previous year. However, net income for the period reached approximately $2.0 billion. While revenue dipped slightly, this profit figure indicates resilience compared to the previous year, when net income was closer to $2.5 billion.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Kimberly-Clark carries a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 4.9x. This indicates a greater reliance on debt than on equity in its capital structure, as total liabilities are significantly higher than shareholders' equity. The current ratio is close to 0.7x, suggesting that short-term liabilities exceed short-term assets. On a cash basis, the company generated free cash flow of roughly $1.6 billion, the cash left over after operating activities and capital expenditures are settled.

Industry observers note that hershey faces intense competition in the global snacking landscape, where rivals' potential integration of artificial intelligence could shift market dynamics. The company is also vulnerable to price volatility in key commodities, especially cocoa, which can squeeze net margin if costs cannot be passed to consumers. Furthermore, Hershey must manage the integration of newly introduced acquisitions like LesserEvil while navigating potential supply chain disruptions or labor strikes.

Recent findings suggest that kimberly-Clark is navigating the financial impact of substantial debt incurred to acquire Kenvue. Successfully integrating these operations and capturing expected synergies is critical to its long-term health. The business also contends with pressure from private-label brands and fluctuations in raw material prices, such as pulp and petroleum. If a major pulp supplier such as Suzano (SUZ +1.09%) experiences market shifts, it could impact Kimberly-Clark's manufacturing costs and overall profitability.

Kimberly-Clark appears to be the more affordable option for investors, trading at a significantly lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

While neither of these mature consumer goods stocks offers major multibagger potential anytime soon, Hershey and Kimberly-Clark present alluring 3.3% and 4.6% dividend yields, respectively, alongside stable operations. Though KMB stock's dividend yield is higher, it might be the more "swing-for-the-fences" style investment between the two companies, primarily because it offers potential upside from its hefty Kenvue acquisition.

According to recent reports, if Kimberly-Clark can successfully integrate its $49 billion acquisition of Kenvue and its wide array of global brands (such as Band-Aid, Tylenol, Listerine, Zyrtec, and Pepcid), it could soar past its meager forward P/E ratio of 16. This is especially true because management believes adjusted earnings per share will grow in the mid- to high-single digits over the next couple of years.

In a recent development, however, I would only consider buying The Hershey Company because I believe the stock offers better long-term compounding potential. Hershey has an unshakable chocolate business, a promptly growing salty snacks unit that it expects to become the No. 2 player over time, and ample international expansion potential.

While GLP-1s pose a threat to Hershey's operations, I think this fear is overdone, as the manufacturer could, counterintuitively, thrive on the peptide's rise to prominence, since miniaturization and smaller-pack sales typically offer higher margins for Hershey. Furthermore, Hershey boasts a better track record of integrating acquisitions, maintains a healthier balance sheet, and has more room to keep raising its dividend payments.

Ultimately, I don't love either stock's odds of beating the market over the next decade, but Hershey could be a great steady-Eddie pick for investors seeking a growing dividend in an increasingly volatile investing environment as we approach 2027.

Mercedes’ New Point-to-Point Driver Assist Helped Me Overcome My Fear of Driving

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “This can go one of two ways,” I think as I slide behind the wheel.
  • As someone who rarely drives – and doesn’t even own a car – in San Francisco, I was eager to see whether Mercedes-Benz’s newly introduced point-to-point driving assistance system could ease my anxiety as I navigated the city’s notoriously challenging streets.
  • After an hour of weaving through these complex environments, I walked away feeling more at ease than when I started.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“This can go one of two ways,” I think as I slide behind the wheel. “Either this makes city driving a lot less intimidating, or I regret ever giving it a try.”.

As someone who rarely drives – and doesn’t even own a car – in San Francisco, I was eager to see whether Mercedes-Benz’s newly introduced point-to-point driving assistance system could ease my anxiety as I navigated the city’s notoriously challenging streets. How would it handle the many four-way stops, steep inclines, pedestrians, cyclists and double-parked robotaxis?

After an hour of weaving through these complex environments, I walked away feeling more at ease than when I started. That’s largely because I barely had to lift a finger – or a foot.

I got an early opportunity to try Mercedes-Benz’s new point-to-point driver assistance system, MB.Drive Assist Pro, which will roll out to select California customers in December before expanding to the rest of the US next year. The Level 2 system handles functions like steering, braking and acceleration, but the driver has to be attentive and ready to take over at any moment. However, I hardly ever needed to.

According to recent reports, as I made my way through San Francisco’s Financial District, Marina and North Beach in a Mercedes-Benz GLC 400, I repeatedly had to resist the urge to tap the brakes, press the accelerator or grab the steering wheel out of instinct. But within minutes, my apprehension had given way to awe at just how much the system could handle and how little I needed to do. With MB.Drive Assist Pro engaged, I watched as the vehicle obeyed traffic signals, yielded the right of way and even maneuvered around stalled robotaxis. Occasionally, I had to briefly place my hands on the wheel so it would know I was paying attention, but I didn’t find it bothersome at all.

It has been revealed that there were moments when I had to take control. At one intersection, a pedestrian was preparing to cross, but the system persisted in making a right turn. (The death glare I got was a sign I needed to take over and tap the brakes.) Further down the road, I grabbed the wheel to steer around a parked truck unloading cargo. Other times, my patience was tested as the car came to a complete stop at every stop sign (rolling stops are my forte, sorry not sorry). To its credit, though, the vehicle subtly asserted itself at four-way stops by inching forward as we waited for our turn.

Unlike Level 4 robotaxi services like Waymo and Zoox, Level 2 systems like MB.Drive Assist Pro aren’t fully autonomous, but can take some of the stress out of everyday driving, particularly in dense urban environments.

In a recent development, tesla’s so-called Full Self-Driving (Supervised) offers similar capabilities, navigating city streets, maneuvering around obstacles, making turns, changing lanes and responding to traffic signals, while still requiring driver supervision. Other systems like GM’s Super Cruise, Ford BlueCruise and BMW Highway Assistant offer hands-free driving on compatible roads, but are primarily designed for use on highways rather than complex city streets.

A feature like MB.Drive Assist Pro could not only bring increasingly advanced driver assistance technology to more car owners but also lay the groundwork for a future in which autonomous driving becomes more common in personally owned vehicles.

“We’ve clearly shown that the autonomous driving sector is an area that we will continue to develop and [be] involved in, and being one of the first companies to offer a system like you guys experienced today highlights that we’re committed to be in that space and continue to grow,” Jason Hoff, CEO of Mercedes-Benz North America, said during a reporter roundtable following the demos.

According to recent reports, MB.Drive Assist Pro uses 27 sensing components, including 10 cameras, five radar sensors and 12 ultrasonic sensors scattered throughout the vehicle. This hardware is right now available on certain 2027 Mercedes vehicles, including CLA Electric, GLE, GLS and S-Class cars. Starting with 2028 models, the organization says more of its US passenger vehicles will be equipped to support the latest feature.

Nvidia’s Alpamayo Stack powers the vehicle’s autonomous driving capabilities, using AI to interpret complex road scenarios and reason through driving decisions. It works alongside Nvidia’s Halos safety tech, including Halos OS, which provides safety guardrails to help ensure the vehicle follows the rules of the road, like stopping at a red light or waiting for an intersection to clear before crossing.

According to recent reports, with Level 2 driving, there’s a mental hurdle that drivers like me will need to overcome and a certain degree of control we’ll have to relinquish to let the system do its thing. For instance, I sometimes found myself getting nervous as the car confidently moved into the oncoming lane to pass a stalled vehicle, even with approaching traffic. I was assured by the Mercedes team that the system can determine whether there’s enough room to safely squeeze through and otherwise wouldn’t attempt the move. Still, it’s not something I’d personally feel comfortable doing if I were in full control.

It has been revealed that some of this simply comes down to a learning curve. Over the hour I spent behind the wheel, I found myself feeling less anxious and more trusting of the system. I’d imagine that confidence would only grow with repeated use of MB.Drive Assist Pro, so drivers can feel less apprehensive about the car taking the lead, even if some decisions still occasionally give them pause.

It has been revealed that MB.Drive Assist Pro will be available nationwide starting next year, with one-month, one-year and three-year subscription options. It’ll come to eligible Mercedes-Benz models including the 2026 CLA electric sedan, 2027 CLA sedan, 2027 GLC electric SUV, 2027 GLE SUV and coupe, 2027 GLS SUV and 2027 S-Class sedan. The system rolled out in China alongside the latest CLA in late 2025. The upcoming rollout will bring it to the US and Germany as well.

Recent findings suggest that customers can factory-order MB.Drive Assist Pro, or purchase it digitally through the Mercedes-Benz store; it will be delivered as an over-the-air patch. Mercedes hasn’t yet shared pricing.

Sources indicate that mercedes is also bringing hands-free highway driving to the US in spring 2027. I had the chance to try out that tech early as well, which proved to be an even bigger test of my trust.

Recent findings suggest that as I drove from Alameda, across the Bay from San Francisco, onto Interstate 880 in a GLS 580, I took a deep breath and prepared to hand over some control to the car. After pressing the Resume button on the steering wheel (or adjusting the cruise control speed), I could activate Hands-Free Highway Assist. The feature comes with a few restrictions: you have to be on a freeway, not in an exit lane and away from construction zones or particularly sharp curves. You also can’t be driving faster than 85 mph.

Industry observers note that hands-Free Highway Assist lets you kick back a bit as the vehicle drives, slowing down and speeding up with traffic. A capability called Proactive Lane Change Assist can automatically switch lanes to overtake a slower vehicle or approach an upcoming exit based on the navigation route.

Industry observers note that as with MB.Drive Assist Pro, you have to watch the road and be ready to take over at any time while using Hands-Free Highway Assist. Given the high stakes and high speeds, I wasn’t as hands-off with the highway driving feature as I was in the urban environment. Driving on the highway already feels nerve-wracking to me even when I’m in full control, so I couldn’t quite overcome the mental hurdle of letting go, physically and metaphorically, for more than about a minute at a time. I’d activate the feature, panic, then reactivate it. (Clearly, I’m a huge thrill seeker.).

One key hurdle is that it can be difficult to know when Hands-Free Highway Assist has been activated. An icon appears on the dashboard showing a green steering wheel with gray hands and two As on each side when the feature is available. Those hands will disappear when the feature is active, leaving only the green steering wheel and As. The icon turns red when you need to take over. Still, it was a little tricky to tell when the feature had correctly been enabled and when I hadn’t yet met all the requirements. Again, part of this is the learning curve, but it’s a substantial lesson to learn at 65 mph.

Sources indicate that still, when I was brave enough to activate the feature, it was impressive to witness the vehicle smoothly weaving across lanes on its own and following the flow of traffic, especially when I had the chance to try it again later in the afternoon on the S 580E. It seems like a handy capability that can make long-haul journeys and daily commutes a little less miserable.

According to recent reports, hands-Free Highway Assist will be available in the US in the spring, and pricing has yet to be determined. An early access program will give select California customers the chance to access the feature next month, alongside MB.Drive Assist Pro. Hands-Free Highway Assist will be on vehicles that support MB.OS (Mercedes’ in-house operating system) as part of the MB.Drive Assist offering, which already includes Steering Assist, Lane Change Assist and Proactive Lane Change Assist. The new feature will arrive via an over-the-air enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that after a day of stepping outside my comfort zone in more ways than one, it was fascinating to get a glimpse of where automotive technology is headed – and how it could make everyday drives, even the more stressful ones, feel a little less daunting. But for now, I hopped into an Uber and returned to my usual routine of avoiding the driver’s seat.

According to recent reports, oura has entered into an agreement to acquire AI primary care company Counsel Health for $625 million. The acquisition of Counsel Health, which was already a partner in the Oura app, will give owners access to Counsel’s in-house physicians and 24/7 medical AI.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

The Oura Ring has evolved from its beginnings as a sleep tracker to what its CEO, Tom Hale, calls “a doctor in your pocket.” The company has its sights set on making the device a continuous medical companion, and Counsel’s acquisition is one way it’s furthering that mission.

Oura employs its 24/7 health monitoring to recognize potential deviations from a user’s biometric baseline, and the partnership will build on those capabilities by adding more clinical guidance through Counsel Health.

The partnership will also connect members with Counsel Health’s medical AI and in-house physicians to address timely health problems, support, or “prescriptions for episodic health conditions,” the press release stated. The acquisition offers specialty and chronic care for chronic conditions, like reproductive, aging, and cardiometabolic-related conditions.

In a recent development, “Oura tells members what’s happening in their bodies, and Counsel helps them act on it. This combination expands our addressable market and deepens the value we deliver to every member,” David Shuman, executive chairman of Oura, said in a press release.

This is the third acquisition Oura has made this year, following its acquisition of Galen AI, a conversational and personal health platform that connects smart ring data to medical records, and Doublepoint AI, an AI‑driven, biometric and gesture recognition company that could add voice or gesture controls to Oura’s next smart ring.

Also: Before you buy a smart ring, consider what you’re giving up.

The Counsel Health deal is expected to close by the end of the year. It’s unknown whether access to Counsel Health physicians or the 24/7 medical AI will be included in an Oura app subscription.

Sources indicate that tech companies have a growing appetite for health tech startups. Last year, Samsung declared a similar acquisition of Xealth, a care platform that connects more than 500 hospitals with 70 digital health centers. The acquisition, according to Samsung VP of digital health Praveen Raja, furthers Samsung’s mission to connect the healthcare landscape, from symptom detection to care provider connection.

Recent findings suggest that one of the Oura Ring’s superpowers is its ability to detect developing illnesses or deviations from my biometric baseline (a spiked resting heart rate, a higher body temperature) before I feel those symptoms. I’ve written about how my Oura Ring detected an illness earlier this year, one day before I began to feel sick.

Also: I should’ve listened to my Oura Ring when it warned me about my health.

According to recent reports, when Oura has flagged these concerns to me, I take them seriously, even as my care provider — to whom I show this data — may shrug them off. The Counsel Health acquisition enables medical AI and in-house physicians to contextualize your biometrics when you are sick or managing a chronic condition.

Will this acquisition help ease the demand for urgent care clinics? As a regular visitor to and hater of my Brooklyn CityMD, I hope so. It is notoriously difficult to get a same-day, in-person appointment with a primary care provider in New York because of high demand and a stretched-thin healthcare system, which often leaves urgent care as the only in-person option for patients.

The press release notes that people could ask physicians for prescriptions. I’m thinking that if I get another bad cold this winter, I could go to my Oura app for help and symptom management instead of CityMD. Making a physician readily available to Oura users could, in theory, reduce dependence on primary or urgent care providers.

Will Your S&P 500 Index Fund Be Forced to Buy Anthropic? Here’s What the Rules Say.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anthropic is about to become one of the largest public companies in the world.
  • Industry observers note that that raises a question for the millions of people who own an index fund in a retirement account.
  • If you own an S&P 500 index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -0.15%).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic is about to become one of the largest public companies in the world. While we don't know exactly what the IPO price will be, or what its stock price will be when it starts trading, at the top of its $70 to $78 price range, the tech giant would be valued at roughly $1.4 trillion. That's bigger than all but a select few U.S. companies.

Industry observers note that that raises a question for the millions of people who own an index fund in a retirement account. If you own an S&P 500 fund, will you automatically end up owning Anthropic? The short answer is no, at least not for a while. But there's a lot more to unpack.

If you own an S&P 500 index fund like the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -0.15%). The S&P 500 isn't simply the 500 largest U.S. companies. If it were, Anthropic would clearly qualify. A committee selects its members and has eligibility rules. A company generally has to be public for 12 months; it needs positive earnings under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) in its most recent four quarters and in its latest quarter, and sufficient shares must trade publicly. In June, S&P Dow Jones Indices specifically stated it would keep those rules in place for megacap IPOs such as SpaceX (SPCX +2.22%), OpenAI, and Anthropic.

Anthropic fails the profitability test by a wide margin, at least on paper. It reported a $104 billion net loss for the first nine months of 2026. Most of that, about $94 billion, came from non-cash charges tied to the rising value of its convertible notes and similar securities, and its operating loss was a much smaller $1.26 billion. Even if its GAAP results improve rapidly after the IPO, the one-year waiting period means the earliest it could join is late 2027.

Sources indicate that on the other hand, if you own a Nasdaq-100 fund like the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ -0.17%), the answer is probably yes, and soon. Nasdaq adopted a fast-entry rule in May that tests a large latest listing on its seventh trading day and allows it to join the index after about 15 trading days. That's how SpaceX joined the Nasdaq-100 less than a month after its June debut. Anthropic is listing on Nasdaq, so it could be in the index by early December.

Let's be clear. None of this tells you whether Anthropic is a good investment, and newly public companies tend to be volatile in their first year. Index inclusion can trigger a burst of buying from funds that must own the stock, but that's a short-term effect, not a reason to own a manufacturer for the long run.

Having said all that, the takeaway for most investors is simple. If you want to own Anthropic in its first few weeks after going public, you'll need to buy it directly or own a Nasdaq-100 fund once it's added. If you'd rather wait and see how it performs as a public firm first, your S&P 500 fund will keep you on the sidelines for at least another year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From left to right: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8, Google Pixel 11, Google Pixel 11 Pro XL.

Google Fi wireless customers with Pixel phones just got a serious upgrade to their mobile and Wi-Fi connections for free.

Here’s how the newly introduced mobile connection feature works: if your main connection slows or becomes unstable, Fi will automatically move to a secondary connection. This not only means you’ll have the fastest option when your connection is good, but you’ll have fewer dead zones when service is limited.

Also: I compared Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T 5G coverage on a road trip – and the winner surprised me.

The feature will run on MEP (Multiple Enabled Profiles) technology, which allows a single eSIM chip to host and run multiple SIM profiles simultaneously. Footnotes in Google’s release note that you’ll need to have “any non-Fi SIMs disabled.”.

Google Fi originally offered automatic switching between two networks when the service debuted a decade ago, but it was between Sprint and T-Mobile, which merged in 2020. Google didn’t reveal what the “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks” were, but ZDNET has reached out to ask. The service usually runs on T-Mobile. Along with T-Mobile, the three biggest carriers are AT&T and Verizon, so it’s likely the second carrier is one of those.

Also: 6 default Pixel 11 settings I changed that made a big difference – and why.

This feature is also coming to Samsung phones running One UI 9 or higher and select modern Motorola phones.

Both of these features, Google explained, are available internationally and are included on Unlimited Premium and Flexible plans at no extra cost.

We see some seasonality in Johnson & Johnson's business from that, with Q1 revenue ticking down compared to prior quarters. According to recent reports, revenue trend is the most obvious figure for investors to examine when considering a stock. The chart indicates that one business is thriving while the other is seeking to regain its footing.

  • The Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 is a multi-purpose piece of hardware made by Nabu Casa, the manufacturer behind official Home Assistant hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that home Assistant is perhaps the most versatile smart home automation system of them all, thanks to the extreme customization power it offers. Today, a tiny, newly introduced box-shaped device is giving Home Assistant users a way to make their existing electronics smarter, rather than replacing them to keep up with the times.

Also: Ring’s newly introduced drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things.

The Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 is a multi-purpose piece of hardware made by Nabu Casa, the manufacturer behind official Home Assistant hardware. The device brings together several connectivity options, including RS-232 serial for older TVs and other equipment, and the ability to connect older stereo systems and amplifiers to modern multi-room audio setups.

Recent findings suggest that “The most sustainable device is the one you already own,” said Paulus Schoutsen, founder of Home Assistant and Nabu Casa. “No device should be left behind because it doesn’t have smart capabilities, or worst of all, its cloud services get turned off.

With the AUX-2, Home Assistant is joining the fight against planned obsolescence and abandoned cloud services.

In a recent development, modern smart home systems have a major drawback: they exclude working electronics simply because they weren’t designed to integrate with today’s smart home platforms. This is the problem that the AUX-2 addresses.

Instead of buying a new stereo system with smart features, consumers can use the $69 AUX-2 to make the devices they already own smarter, more connected, and easier to control.

According to recent reports, A single AUX-2 can control multiple devices, depending on how they’re connected and the interfaces they use. The device’s limit has more to do with the number of physical connections required.

Also: How I open-sourced my smart home – and ditched Google for Siri.

Sources indicate that the AUX-2 lets you connect two serial-controlled devices directly through the RS-232 ports. The USB port can act as an expansion for compatible adapters. You can place one AUX-2 on an entertainment center and connect an older stereo and TV, then use another AUX-2 elsewhere in your house for additional equipment with physical serial connections.

According to Home Assistant, with an AUX-2, you can control an old AV receiver without the original app, have an older TV respond to commands without relying on its manufacturer’s cloud servers, or integrate existing audio equipment into modern multiroom sound systems.

This way, consumers won’t need to trash a functional piece of equipment simply because the manufacturer stops supporting it.

Aside from RS-232 serial, the AUX-2 also supports Bluetooth, Z-Wave, USB, PoE, and Wi-Fi for connectivity.

Also: 5 smart home gadgets I actually recommend, after years of testing.

  • Now he’s adding one more major role to his portfolio: James Bond.
  • Amazon MGM Studios named the English actor the new 007 on Monday, ending the hunt to replace Daniel Craig, who played Bond from 2006 to 2021 in five films: Casino Royale, Quantum of Solace, Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s safe to say Robert Pattinson is on a generational run, starring in The Odyssey, The Drama, Die My Love and Primetime just this year alone. Having previously played Edward Cullen in The Twilight Saga and Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ The Batman (and gearing up for a role in Dune: Part Three this December), he’s no stranger to major film franchises.

Now he’s adding one more major role to his portfolio: James Bond.

Amazon MGM Studios named the English actor the new 007 on Monday, ending the hunt to replace Daniel Craig, who played Bond from 2006 to 2021 in five films: Casino Royale, Quantum of Solace, Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die.

Several other British A-list actors were speculated to be in the running for the role, including Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor, but it seems Amazon MGM Studios is banking on a significant-name actor with a proven record of box-office success for its lead. Pattinson’s connection to director Denis Villeneuve, who was also director of the Dune trilogy, likely played a role in the decision, too.

“To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” Pattinson mentioned in a statement. “I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

Read more: Ready to Watch a James Bond Movie? These Are My Top Recommendations for You.

It has been revealed that pattinson is the eighth actor to play James Bond on screen. The full list of actors who have portrayed 007 includes Sean Connery (1962-1983), David Niven for one (unofficial) film in 1967, George Lazenby for one film in 1969, Roger Moore (1973-1985), Timothy Dalton (1987-1989), Pierce Brosnan (1995-2002) and Craig (2006-2021).

Industry observers note that the next Bond film has not yet been titled and is not expected to begin filming until 2027, with a 2028 release date. Steven Knight (Peaky Blinders) has been brought on as the screenwriter, with Amy Pascal (Project Hail Mary) and David Heyman (Harry Potter series) producing and Tanya Lapointe (Dune trilogy) executive producing.

Sources indicate that amazon formally closed its acquisition of MGM Studios in 2022 for $8.45 billion, giving it the rights to distribute all James Bond films. In 2025, Amazon MGM Studios unveiled a joint venture with longtime franchise producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli to remain co-owners of the franchise, while ultimately giving Amazon MGM Studios creative control.

According to recent reports, “Few films carry the kind of anticipation that comes with James Bond, and we have strived to honor the passionate fans, the legacy and the future of this iconic character,” said Courtenay Valenti, head of film at Amazon MGM Studios. “We are thrilled to officially welcome Robert Pattinson as our 007 and are confident he will bring something truly special to this role. Robert, Denis, Amy, David and Tanya are embarking on an amazing adventure together.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Have you ever thrown away groceries that spoiled before you got around to using them?
  • It’s easy to let things go to waste and accumulate more than we need.
  • Use Less Stuff Day, which lands on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Have you ever thrown away groceries that spoiled before you got around to using them? Or bought a newly introduced jacket despite already having half a dozen in your closet?

It’s easy to let things go to waste and accumulate more than we need.

Use Less Stuff Day, which lands on Nov. 19 this year, encourages us to rethink our consumption habits and make more mindful, environmentally friendly choices.

That might mean squeezing every last drop out of what you’ve got, finding creative ways to reuse things or simply buying less.

I keep a couple of simple tricks up my sleeve to extend the life of my family’s clothing: OxiClean soaks and basic sewing skills. You’d be surprised by how many things you can salvage with a little cleaning and mending.

In a recent development, I asked my fellow Nerds to share some of the ways they reduce waste and unnecessary spending. Maybe you’ll pick up an idea or two.

Pamela de la Fuente, managing editor: My husband grew up with a “make what’s in the house” kinda family. I didn’t. But this weekend while looking for spaghetti I found some crispy rice cereal, and I knew we had marshmallows from a bonfire a few weeks ago so I stated, “I’m going to make crispy rice treats with this for the kids and get rid of this cereal.” (Surprisingly, it was not stale.) I still had cereal left, so I added it to some chocolate protein bars I love to make and my son said, “These are 9 out of 10. Usually they are 7 out of 10!”.

Karen Gaudette Brewer, head of content: I’m a big “make big batches of food and freeze it” person, so I can drive everyone nuts reminding them that we really do have food at home. That freezer also holds grated lemon zest and cubes of those last little bits of chicken broth and wine so that I can easily make pan sauces and not waste that last half cup of goodness.

It has been revealed that jessica Cano, content coordinator: I save the tops from strawberries after cutting them for my kids. We use some to make strawberry balsamic vinegar, some to make strawberry syrup and the rest go in the freezer to be used for smoothies. Keeps me from having to buy frozen fruit and multiple vinegars.

Industry observers note that pantry shopping can result in less food in the trash and fewer trips to the grocery store. It can also make experimenting with newly introduced recipes a little more exciting. Take a page from Managing Editor Athena Cocoves, who says, “Sometimes we pretend we're on ‘Chopped.’”.

Ryan Brady, lead writer: Rotating toys with our kids has helped them get more enjoyment out of the same toys versus constantly buying newly introduced toys. We put a bunch of toys they're bored with in a bin, and months later, take one out and bam — it's like a new toy all over again!

Kim Lowe, head of content: I invested a whole $12 in a lint remover last winter that transformed all my old sweaters into almost fresh!

Laura McMullen, editor: Almost all of my kids’ clothes are thrifted or hand-me-downs. My friend group of parents has kids from age 2 to 7, all of whom are about six months apart. We’ve developed a hearty clothing exchange. It’s fun to see my friends' kids wear hand-me-downs that we got from my brother’s family almost 10 years ago.

It has been revealed that look for other ways to salvage your belongings or get them secondhand. That might include watching a vacuum repair tutorial on YouTube, borrowing books from the library or purchasing used tools from Facebook Marketplace. The goal: Keep more stuff in circulation and out of landfills.

Abby Doyle, lead writer: Composting isn’t as fussy as it seems. Once you get into it, you start seeing would-be waste as stuff to feed your new backyard buddy. Junk mail, paper bags, slimy spring mix … it’s all food for my “pet dirt.” And my garden has legit never looked better.

Yuliya Goldshteyn, editor: Instead of throwing away kid art, I reuse it as wrapping paper throughout the year. Bespoke gift wrapping for everyone! I haven’t bought gift wrap for five years now.

Industry observers note that caitlin Constantine, editor: I repurpose glass jars and plastic containers. It always seemed like such a pity to throw perfectly good containers into the recycling after one use, so now I reuse them before I recycle them.

Before you toss something, ask yourself, “Is there another way I can use this?” An old T-shirt makes a good cleaning rag, for example.

Being resourceful often means getting as much mileage as possible out of what you have.

Also: You can now restore Windows 11 even if it can’t boot up – here’s how.

On its support page to the November update designated KB5132061, Microsoft revealed and explained this latest problem.

In a recent development, windows users who installed the November preview update released on October 28 may run into a glitch when trying to install the actual November update released on November 10. In this case, the installation may fail to complete. Your PC might repeatedly try to install the update or you may simply see an error code such as 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993.

I can confirm the problem. I installed the preview revision on one of my Windows 11 virtual machines. Trying to then install the actual November update triggered the installation error.

Sources indicate that if you’re in the same boat, what can you do to fix this dilemma? Just be patient.

Also: Windows finally gets a built-in internet speed test tool – how to try it.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft promises that all affected PCs should receive repairs within 24 to 48 hours starting from November 11, 1pm ET. For this, make sure your PC is connected to the internet and is set up to receive updates via Windows Patch. Head to Settings and select Windows Update. You may already find the November update known as 2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974) available again. If so, select it to install it, and the process should work now.

In a recent development, I tried this on my virtual machine, and the November patch installed without a hitch. But if you still bump into errors, check out Microsoft’s support page on troubleshooting problems updating Windows.

Here’s how the update process works.

Microsoft typically releases each monthly Windows update in two phases.

In a recent development, first, there’s an optional preview upgrade that kicks off around the end of the previous month. This one is considered a non-security update because it contains only feature changes. In this case, the preview update for November was released on October 28. Labeled KB5127936, this one unveiled the newly introduced customizable right-click menu, Cloud rebuild option, and other feature changes.

Also: You can change Windows settings directly from a search now.

Second, there’s the actual mandatory Patch Tuesday update that contains both security patches and the non-security changes. Here, the November KB5132061 update was rolled out on November 10.

The preview updates are designed for IT administrators, software testers, and others who want an early look. That means they aren’t always fully baked and may contain a few bugs. But since they pop up in Windows Enhancement, anyone can install them.

In a recent development, the actual Patch Tuesday updates are for all Windows users. In this case, there seemed to be an incompatibility or other conflict between the two updates that Microsoft then had to resolve.

It has been revealed that the images seen here are taken with the phone’s various built-in camera modes, largely the black and white mode, as I love the dramatic, filmic look it produces. Sources indicate that taken using one of the phone’s built-in color styles, I love the vibrancy in this shot. The reds really pop, while the wider angle of the main camera emphasizes the tunnel effect of the alleyway, drawing the eye to the person and their dog.

I may be spoiling the rest of the images here by saying that this is my absolute favorite shot I’ve taken, but there we go. I took this using one of the dedicated black-and-white modes, and I think the tones here are perfect. Excellent dynamic range and contrast, and just the right amount of film grain. I positioned the figure between the buildings and had the phone almost on the floor to turn the rain-soaked tiles into a reflective surface to add some drama to this scene. I then applied a wide cinematic crop in post to give it that extra edge. Lovely stuff.

Most of my favorite photos with the phone were taken using the black-and-white mode. It’s no surprise; I shoot in black and white very often on my Leica Q3 43, and I used the monochrome mode for my favorite shots with Xiaomi’s Leitzphone earlier in the year.

The phone captures excellent black-and-white photos at night, too.

Industry observers note that and by exposing for the bright highlights in this scene, I was able to create this stark, moody image of my handsome orange cat, Toulouse. Is he the best cat you’ve ever seen? Of course he is.

It has been revealed that back in color, this UFO that had presumably crash-landed in this Parisian market looks great in this filmic color mode. The oranges and reds pop against the other tones in this scene.

While this quick street portrait is similarly punchy.

It has been revealed that I used manual mode here, taking full control over the white balance and exposure settings to achieve the tones I wanted. It’s a great-looking shot with excellent dynamic range. Xiaomi’s phone doesn’t appear to go too hard with its software processing either, meaning that even fine details look quite natural. Other Android phone-makers could take note.

As with the photo of Toulouse the cat, I exposed for the highlights here, forcing the rest of the scene under this bridge into shadow. As a result, it looks moody and dramatic but crucially it also looks exactly as I hoped it would. Many phones would try to artificially lift the shadows here, which would ruin the vibe I was going for.

I took this with the phone’s telephoto zoom lens, aiming to focus more on the digger as the subject and use the water for reflection. I love how this shot looks, especially in black and white, as the cloud detail behind it is especially noticeable.

While here I used the full wide angle of the main camera in order to create a lot of negative space around the figures, emphasizing the size of the building around them.

That building was Le Grande Arche in Paris and despite it being a miserably cold, wet and cloudy day I think the phone has captured a satisfyingly stark scene here.

I don’t like flying, so I distracted myself on the flight out to Paris by taking photos of things with the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, including this man having a look out of the window.
