Geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and soaring bond yields weighed on global markets this past week. And investors are closely assessing the valuations of artificial intelligence stocks amid concerns about the sustainability of high spending on AI infrastructure.

Despite those continued challenges, top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the prospects of several stocks due to their long-run growth potential and exposure to lucrative business lines, including AI.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Sources indicate that cybersecurity tech giant CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) is this week's first stock pick. The company is scheduled to announce fiscal second-quarter results on August 26.

Ahead of Q2 FY27 earnings, Truist analyst Junaid Siddiqui reiterated a buy rating on CrowdStrike stock and raised his price target to $245 from $187.50. Following CrowdStrike's impressive fiscal first-quarter performance and guidance raise, Siddiqui expects another strong quarter.

Industry observers note that the 5-star analyst's optimism is backed by continued strength in Falcon Flex adoption and encouraging large deal activity. Siddiqui also cited continued momentum across emerging products. With the FY27 outlook assuming persistent strength in CrowdStrike's net upcoming annual recurring revenue (ARR), Siddiqui is more focused on the longevity of key growth catalysts such as Falcon Flex adoption, platform consolidation and AI-led demand.

The analyst highlighted that talks with partners were encouraging, with pipeline generation and momentum in large deals remaining healthy in the fiscal second quarter despite tough, year-over-year comparisons.

"We continue to view CrowdStrike as one of the primary beneficiaries of platform consolidation, though we expect investors to remain focused on competitive dynamics and whether current growth levels represent a new baseline or a period of demand acceleration," the analyst stated.

Industry observers note that siddiqui ranks No. 226 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 80% of the time, delivering an average return of about 40%. See CrowdStrike Financials on TipRanks.

Shares of personal computer maker Dell Technologies (DELL) have rallied 251% this year, driven by strong demand for AI servers. Recently, Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani reiterated a buy rating on DELL and raised his price target to $550 from $500.

The 5-star analyst contends that while Dell's AI compute segment is getting investors' attention, the organization's Storage business is underappreciated and well-positioned to drive revenue and profit acceleration. Daryanani expects the storage business to see higher demand once enterprises start to bring workload back on-premises.

The analyst highlighted that Dell's Storage business, estimated to account for only 10% of FY27 revenue, is one of the factors that could help improve profit margins, given its higher profitability compared to AI servers. Daryanani estimates that the Storage business's operating margin is presently in the low-20% range, while margins for the AI server and traditional server businesses are in the mid-single-digit and mid-teens range, respectively.

Overall, Daryanani views the Storage business as an notable catalyst for three reasons: Dell has one of the broadest storage portfolios in the industry; Storage has a significantly higher margin profile than AI servers; and the shift toward proprietary, software-defined storage and AI-focused platforms.

"We think DELL's storage business is becoming increasingly strategic as AI infrastructure deployments move beyond GPU procurement and toward full stack + AI-ready architectures," noted Daryanani.

In a recent development, daryanani ranks No. 19 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 71% of the time, delivering an average return of 38.70%. See Dell Technologies Statistics on TipRanks.

SanDisk (SNDK) is benefiting from AI-driven demand for its memory and storage products. Following the tech giant's 2026 Investor Day event, J.P. Morgan analyst Harlan Sur resumed research coverage of SNDK with a buy rating (it was earlier, "Not Rated") and a price target of $2,250.

In a recent development, the 5-star analyst believes SanDisk is well-positioned to capitalize on a structural inflection reached in NAND demand, driven by strong growth in AI inference. Sur's bullishness is based on three key factors.

Sources indicate that first, Sur believes that SanDisk's New Business Model (NBM) framework (or long-term agreements) has enhanced its margin profile and reduced cyclicality. SNDK's eight signed NBMs represent a total contract value of $94 billion and a gross margin of about 80%, even at the floor pricing.

It has been revealed that second, Sur highlighted the growing NAND market and expects the total addressable market to surge from about $70 billion in calendar year 2025 to over $300 billion in 2026 and about $500 billion in 2027. Importantly, the analyst noted that data centers are the largest driver of NAND growth, as hyperscalers increasingly deploy flash for AI inference workloads.

Finally, Sur is optimistic on SanDisk due to its technology dominance. The company's BiCS10 technology is sampling ahead of schedule and has 65% more bits per wafer than BiCS8, the analyst noted. Also, Sur expects SanDisk's High Bandwidth Flash to become a differentiated memory platform for AI inference.

"Layered on top, mgmt's commitment to returning 100% of excess cash flow to shareholders should drive an aggressive share count reduction trajectory that further amplifies EPS growth on a per-share basis," said Sur.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My weekday breakfasts used to come down to a protein smoothie or scrambled eggs, mostly because both are fast.

It has been revealed that poached eggs, my favorite version, stayed on the weekend list because the stovetop method takes more babysitting than I can manage before work. A microwave was the key to changing all that.

Recent findings suggest that now, with just a small bowl of cold water and about a minute of cooking, I get a poached egg with a firm white and a soft yolk, ready to slide onto toast or greens. And it’s the best prep method I’ve found thus far.

This method demands just one minute, one bowl and leaves no mess, save for the quick rinse of a wet mug. The results are surprisingly good and the process is impossible to flub. You can easily tinker with timing to get the exact consistency you’re after.

Industry observers note that so ditch the frying pan or sluggish pot of boiling water. Here’s how to make perfect poached eggs in under 60 seconds.

Read more: Achieve Your Daily Protein Goals With This Simple Visual Guide.

Step 1: Fill a ramekin with a half-cup of salted, room-temperature water. It must be enough to submerge the egg.

You’ll want enough water to submerge the egg but not spill over the top of the ramekin.

Step 2: Crack one egg and carefully drop it into the water, trying not to disturb its structural integrity.

Step 3: Place the ramekin in the microwave and cook on high for about 45 seconds, longer if you prefer a firmer yolk.

Cook the submerged egg for 40 seconds for a runny yolk and closer to a minute for a firm one.

Step 4: Remove the egg gently from the water with a slotted spoon or wire skimmer.

Lift your egg carefully out of the water with a slotted spoon or mesh strainer.

Step 5: Serve over toast or a bed of greens with avocado, hot sauce, chili crisp and other accompaniments.

In one or two tries you’ll be able to fine-tune your poached egg to your perfect doneness and then nail it every time.

Note: The base temperature for any microwave will vary, and thus, cook times may also. Try 40 to 45 seconds for your first effort, then add five-second increments for subsequent tries until you achieve the desired doneness.

I haven’t experienced any egg-related explosions, but a Reddit deep dive into microwave egg poachers unearthed a nugget of advice: Avoid yolk explosions by poking it through with a toothpick.

In a recent development, stick that fluffy puff of protein on a piece of toast with some spinach, top it all with flaky salt, hot sauce or hollandaise and have a cafe-quality breakfast in less time than it takes to brew coffee. You can also use them to top a salad or serve over rice with pickled vegetables and chili crisp for a light lunch.

Recent findings suggest that cooking bacon in the oven is the cleanest method and results in even crispier strips, with no greasy stovetop to clean afterward. A fast water boil with these two pantry ingredients lifts stubborn stains from your best cookware without all the manic scrubbing. Here are nine more cooking hacks that save time, energy, and money.

If you don’t want to cook, this is my favorite prepared meal delivery service for 2025.

A small batch of bacon cooked in the air fryer can be another quick protein value add to your breakfast in the morning and it’s a perfect pairing with your microwave-poached egg.

According to recent reports, you can prevent your egg yolk from exploding by starting with a small increment of time in the microwave, like 45 seconds. If you need to heat the egg more, you can add increments of five seconds as needed. Poking the egg yolk with a toothpick before putting the egg in the microwave may also help prevent an explosion during or after poaching the egg.

Using your microwave to poach eggs is a quick way to get some protein added to your breakfast or lunch, and it’s a completely safe way to cook the egg as long as you add small increments to the microwave timer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in what might be its biggest news in years, Ava Labs, the company that builds the blockchain behind the cryptocurrency Avalanche (AVAX +0.81%), just said on Nov. 9 that it struck a deal with the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) to be the backend infrastructure for settling tokenized stocks on a new 24/7 alternative trading system (ATS), a venue that matches buyers and sellers of securities without registering as a full stock exchange. If the collaboration delivers everything that holders are hoping for, it could well become the spark of a multiyear comeback arc.

The price of Avalanche is still 95% below its all-time high set in 2021, which could lead some investors to imagine that the coin is still a bargain given this development. So is it a screaming buy right now?

It has been revealed that the NYSE's parent company, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE -0.59%), initially announced the new venue back on Jan. 19, describing it as an exchange with 24/7 access to U.S. stocks, instant transaction settlement, and other features like stablecoin-based funding. It's slated to launch in the fourth quarter of this year, pending regulatory approval.

It has been revealed that the NYSE remarked that in its search for a blockchain partner to provide the ledger that clears and settles the exchange's transactions, it wanted a network with predictable transaction costs that could also gate which actors are allowed to participate. The NYSE will run its own custom blockchain built with Avalanche's technology rather than send its transactions over Avalanche's public blockchain network. Those custom networks can charge fees in any token their operator picks. In this case, each network pays 1.33 AVAX coins monthly per computer that verifies transactions (validators), and then the network permanently destroys those coins.

CRYPTO · As of 10:03 AM ET 11/17/26.

The trouble is that such a small fee is practically irrelevant to Avalanche.

Assuming, purely for illustration, that the NYSE chain ran 20 validators, it would burn about 319.2 AVAX per year, which would be worth about $2,289 at the Nov. 16 price. In the 24-hour period ended at noon on Nov. 16, Avalanche's public network collected $17,605 in transaction fees, more than that hypothetical year of burn.

There's no reason to expect that many thousands of validators would ever be needed. Therefore the direct impact of the fee burns from the exchange's activity on the coin's price is almost guaranteed to be minimal.

The bull case for buying Avalanche right now is thus fairly indirect.

The NYSE chain could in theory connect to Avalanche's wider ecosystem, which in turn could push some activity onto the public blockchain. Beyond the small validator fees, that's the main way the deal could reach coin holders.

Scale is the other unknown. ICE describes the platform as a newly introduced venue, so it may handle only a sliver of the NYSE's business. It's also faintly possible that it could handle a large helping of that business.

In a recent development, nonetheless, landing the NYSE as a customer could help Avalanche to get more financial institutions interested in its network. During the next few quarters, watch how much activity there is when the platform rolls out and whether Avalanche or ICE allows AVAX any real role in fees or even staking on the NYSE chain.

If neither happens by mid-2027, this coin is probably not something that is worth buying -- which is the same as the present state of affairs.

Google’s Pixel Tag, the company’s take on an Android-exclusive Bluetooth tracker, is finally here, following its August announcement during the Google I/O developer conference.

Also: Google’s new Android XR glasses have lower ‘creep factor’ than competitors.

Pixel Tag is a complete Bluetooth tracker for Android people that appears less confined to device-specific ecosystems than Samsung’s Smart Tag 3 and Apple’s AirTag.

Industry observers note that however, if you look at Google’s footnotes, the Pixel Tag’s functionality is diminished when an older Android phone is involved. Several of the tracker’s best features require a compatible device running Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, according to Google.

Industry observers note that android 9 and newer encompasses a lot of devices, but Bluetooth 6.0 and newer doesn’t. Here’s what to check before you buy.

Smartphones began shipping with Bluetooth 6.0 in 2025, starting with the Samsung Galaxy S26 Plus and Galaxy S26 Ultra. The following phones also have Bluetooth 6.0:.

If your Android phone is older than any of the listed above, even by a generation, it likely supports Bluetooth 5.3 or 5.4 — not enough for the Pixel Tag’s best features.

It has been revealed that the Pixel Tag’s precision-finding capabilities are powered by Bluetooth Channel Sounding, a key feature introduced in Bluetooth 6.0. Nearly every review I’ve seen of the Pixel Tag, including our own, tests the tracker when paired with a Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 11, or Pixel 11 Pro.

According to recent reports, I assume that Android users whose phones run Android 9.0+ but lack Bluetooth 6.0+ can use the Pixel Tag for very basic, general location tracking. These users may see the tracker’s general location, but Google’s device compatibility footnote appears several times throughout its press release.

The following features require Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, according to Google’s release:.

So, on older Android devices without Android 9.0+ and Bluetooth 6.0+, the following aren’t supported: locating the exact direction and distance of your tracked devices, pinging a tracker when you don’t see it, or giving your tracked devices a custom name.

Also: 3 ways Bluetooth 7 upgrades your devices beyond lossless audio.

In a recent development, additionally, shorter-distance tracking requires an ultra-wideband chip inside your Android phone. Channel Sounding handles distance and direction at longer ranges, while UWB takes over for shorter ranges. Most premium Android phones with Bluetooth 6.0 also have UWB chips, but several of Google’s base-model phones lack a UWB chip.

Samsung’s base-model, A-series, and Z Flip-series phones also lack UWB, resulting in more phones that can’t access the Pixel Tag’s short-range precision finding capabilities.

With all the specs in mind, the Pixel Tag is the best option for people of recent premium flagship Android phones. Those without the latest Bluetooth connectivity will find that the Pixel Tag works like any other Bluetooth tracker, with basic functionality.

Also: These are the closest things to AirTags for Android consumers.

The good thing is that a single Pixel Tag is $30, so it’s not much more expensive than a Tile Tag, and cheaper than a Chipolo Loop. Still, if your phone doesn’t support Bluetooth 6.0, you might be better off looking for a cheaper option until you’re ready to upgrade.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the iPhone Duo‘s biggest drawbacks has just been addressed – mostly.
  • In a recent development, unlike Apple’s other current iPhones, the iPhone Duo lacks Face ID, meaning you have to rely on the noticeably less speedy Touch ID or enter a passcode to unlock the foldable device.
  • In its latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple has added an option to unlock the iPhone Duo using the front camera.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the iPhone Duo‘s biggest drawbacks has just been addressed – mostly.

In a recent development, unlike Apple’s other current iPhones, the iPhone Duo lacks Face ID, meaning you have to rely on the noticeably less speedy Touch ID or enter a passcode to unlock the foldable device. This would be less painful if the Duo didn’t cost $1,999, and if Face ID hadn’t long been a standard feature across the firm’s other iPhones, including its most affordable option.

Now, there’s something of a fix. In its latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple has added an option to unlock the iPhone Duo using the front camera. This should make accessing the phone’s contents more seamless and intuitive.

It has been revealed that until now, my least favorite aspect of using the iPhone Duo has been the inability to unlock using facial recognition – a limitation that stands in stark contrast to the foldable phone’s premium feel. Scanning a fingerprint with Touch ID not only feels antiquated for such a pricey device, but also rather slow. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, by contrast, has a facial recognition feature, as well as fingerprint unlocking that’s much faster than the Duo’s.

It appears Apple heard our cries and is bringing a workaround to the Duo. This new unlocking capability isn’t quite the same as Face ID, a more secure biometric facial recognition and authentication system. Instead, the iPhone Duo will now let you unlock the phone using the selfie camera under slightly more limited conditions to help ensure security.

Read more: Meet the Custom-Built Machine That Has Folded the iPhone Duo 500,000 Times.

Industry observers note that to enable the latest optional unlock feature, go to your Duo’s Settings and toggle it on under Touch ID & Passcode. Because unlocking with the Duo’s front camera isn’t as secure as using Touch ID or Face ID, you’ll need to use Touch ID or enter a passcode after around 45 minutes of inactivity. Touch ID is also required when using Apple Pay or accessing your passwords.

According to recent reports, unlocking with the front camera is possible because of a newly introduced capability in Apple silicon called Secure Exclaves. The iPhone Duo uses this to securely and privately process data of a user’s face and verify the match. That means iOS, apps, people and Apple can’t access the data used to unlock the phone via the front camera.

I admittedly didn’t think this update would arrive on Apple’s first-generation foldable; I assumed we’d just have to cross our fingers and hope for Face ID to land on the next iteration. It’s a relatively small improvement, but one that I think will make the Duo experience a lot more convenient and in line with the phone’s modern design and aesthetics, even if it’s not a full Face ID fix. As much as I thought I could make do with Touch ID, it turned out to be more of a nuisance than I’d anticipated; I’m so used to the speediness of unlocking by simply looking at a phone’s screen and swiping up. So I’m glad there’s a software update to help address that gap on the Duo.

The next iOS 27.3 developer beta also adds the option for the iPhone Duo to automatically lock when someone closes the phone. You can enable this under Settings > Display & Brightness.

Alongside other recent software updates, including the addition of Reachability to make the Duo’s cover screen content easier to access one-handed, and support for Apple Pencil with USB-C, Apple appears poised to continue rolling out features that make the Duo more adaptable.

Google is adding digital home keys to Google Wallet, letting people tap their phones to unlock compatible smart locks. The home key functionality, which will integrate with Google Home, will roll out this month.

Also: This tiny box gives your older tech smart home superpowers.

Sources indicate that apple introduced Home Keys in 2021 with iOS 15, allowing consumers to store digital keys in the Apple Wallet. This lets you tap your iPhone or Apple Watch on the lock to unlock it. More recently, the addition of Express Mode to Apple Home lets users unlock smart locks without first unlocking their iPhones with Face ID.

In a recent development, google’s digital keys use tap-to-unlock via NFC on smart locks. Like the Apple Home Key, you don’t need to unlock your phone to use your digital key, though you can change your verification settings as you wish.

According to recent reports, google’s announcement confirms that the company is embracing Aliro and UWB unlocking technologies as well. UWB unlocking for smart locks is supported on Google Pixel 10 Pro and newer models, as well as select UWB-enabled Samsung Galaxy phones. Aliro is a common standard for compatible smart locks and devices.

It has been revealed that before Google’s announcement, compatible smart locks could be controlled on Android through their accompanying app and Google Home. Smart lock companies also offered their own digital access methods, like NFC cards, Bluetooth, and geolocation.

One digital key will be created for each Google Home, so it can unlock all compatible smart locks in that home. You won’t need to search through digital keys in Google Wallet to find the one for your front door, back door, or bedroom door — just tap your phone and Google Home will recognize the lock as one in your smart home ecosystem.

At launch, Google Wallet will support digital keys for the Aqara U400 with UWB and NFC, and NFC on the Schlage Sense Pro and Nuki Keypad 2.

Google Wallet already supports digital car keys for compatible vehicles.

Lame-Duck Congress Faced With Averting Another Shutdown

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With the midterm election in the rearview and a new Democrat-controlled Congress about to be sworn in Jan.
  • Over the summer, the House of Representatives passed a stopgap bill that would extend government funding at its current level through the December deadline, in a bid to push the funding battle until after midterm elections.
  • Disagreements over spending priorities could once again leave the government facing a shutdown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the midterm election in the rearview and a new Democrat-controlled Congress about to be sworn in Jan. 4, the current class of legislators finds itself working to avoid an impending government shutdown that would start after Dec. 11.

Over the summer, the House of Representatives passed a stopgap bill that would extend government funding at its current level through the December deadline, in a bid to push the funding battle until after midterm elections. The government had been set to run out of money after Sept. 30.

Disagreements over spending priorities could once again leave the government facing a shutdown. Lawmakers face a deadline, with little time to negotiate a longer-term spending deal before the extension expires on Dec. 11. The lame-duck session — the period between the November elections and the start of the new Congress — gives outgoing lawmakers one final opportunity to reach a long-term agreement or extend the deadline into 2027.

It has been revealed that some Senate Democrats are threatening to withhold support for a deal unless it includes restrictions on funding President Donald Trump’s war with Iran. Meanwhile, Trump is urging Senate leaders to use budget reconciliation to fund an additional $350 billion in supplemental defense spending.

However, leaders in both parties are publicly supporting a short-term stopgap that would keep the government funded until after the current lame-duck session ends.

Sources indicate that every year, Congress is supposed to pass 12 spending bills to keep the government’s lights on. These appropriations bills fund those programs already approved by Congress, including defense, the IRS, food assistance, veterans’ benefits and national parks.

According to recent reports, the deadline to fund programs for the next fiscal year is always Oct. 1. Without passing appropriations bills or approving a stopgap that kicks the deadline down the road, the government shuts down.

In the past few funding cycles, Congress has relied on multiple short-term continuing resolutions to keep the government temporarily running.

In 2025, the government shut down for the longest period in U.S. history (Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 43 days) while this year was marked by the longest partial shutdown ever (Feb. 14 to April 30, 76 days). Why didn’t Congress pass the funding bills in 2025? The two parties were deadlocked over Democrats’ ultimately unsuccessful efforts to permanently extend expiring Obamacare subsidies and roll back recent Medicaid cuts in the One Major, Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

A second shutdown — this one partial — began on Feb. 14. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) shut down after lawmakers failed to reach a deal to reform Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) tactics. DHS funding became a flashpoint following the fatal shootings of Renée Good on Jan. 7 by an ICE agent and Alex Pretti on Jan. 24 by a CBP agent, both in Minneapolis. The DHS shutdown followed a four-day partial shutdown that ended Feb. 3.

On April 30, the House passed a bill approved by the Senate to fund most of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The deal fully funded all DHS offices with the exceptions of ICE and Border Patrol. Democrats supported the deal, despite it lacking any of the restrictions on the two agencies that they had been demanding throughout the shutdown.

» MORE: How to prepare for the next government shutdown.

In a recent development, at 43 days, the 2025 government shutdown was the longest in history. There have been 22 shutdowns since 1976 and most are short-lived — a few hours or days, at the most.

Sources indicate that before then, there hadn’t been a shutdown since 2018-2019. That shutdown, which lasted 35 days, arose in a dispute over funding for Trump’s border wall in his first term.

Industry observers note that before that there was a 16-day shutdown in 2013, as negotiations over the Affordable Care Act dragged on. In 1995 and 1996, two shutdowns totaled 26 days.

Federal workers bear the brunt of impact from government shutdowns.

During a shutdown, there are ripple effects on delivery of government services and programs.

National parks may close or operate without services.

Federal student aid application processing could be delayed.

Food and drug inspections will be delayed.

The IRS can’t verify income and Social Security numbers, which could cause delays for some mortgages and other loan approvals, as well as tax refunds.

What will keep running, to a point:.

Flights will still operate, but there could be delays if TSA agents and air traffic controllers, who are considered essential employees, decide to call out of work, leading to staff shortages. Even small shortages can have a big impact: During a 2019 government shutdown, the absence of just 10 air traffic controllers at two airports grounded flights and caused delays for the Eastern Seaboard. (Read more on how the shutdown affects travel.).

Social Security and Medicare will keep going, but some administrative functions may be suspended, and telehealth appointments may be interrupted.

Unemployment benefits will continue — states administer compensation — but there could be application processing delays if the shutdown lasts long enough.

It has been revealed that food benefits through Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and the accompanying WIC program will continue — both run on contingency funds. WIC funding will only last one month, and SNAP could be strained after 30 days, as well.

The postal service — the USPS is not funded by the federal government.

Federal student loan payments — accounts are serviced by private companies.

Public schools will remain open — they’re funded by state and local governments.

Amtrak will continue operations — it is operated by a for-profit company.

See more details on how a government shutdown could impact you. The shutdown has had trickle-down economic effects. One immediate and direct impact during the previous shutdown was a suspension of federal economic data. Most of that data wasn’t released during the shutdown. That’s a problem because the government’s official data releases guide the markets, the Federal Reserve and business decisions.ent’s official data releases guide the markets, the Federal Reserve and business decisions.

So while Rocket Lab hasn't given us a clear date for its first Neutron launch yet, we can optimistically assume it will happen sometime within the first half of 2027 to hit Wall Street's targets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that did SNL just add another legendary fake commercial to the show’s hall of fame? On Saturday night, host John Mulaney and the cast delivered a winning pretaped parody commercial that hit a nerve in more than a few households.

Recent findings suggest that in the ad, Mulaney and others fret about their aging parents. Nursing homes don’t appeal, yet in-home care would cost too much. Fortunately, Mulaney has heard about Sister, “a live-in, 24/7 eldercare provider that is completely free, and also your sister.”.

“I love my mom more than anything,” says another adult son, played by Andrew Dismukes. “That doesn’t mean I want to help her in the bathroom. Sister doesn’t either. But she will, whereas I won’t. That’s the Sister difference!”.

Jane Wickline plays a frantic sister who drops everything, quits her job, breaks her lease, and moves halfway across the country to take care of her elderly dad (Tommy Brennan, ironically one of the youngest cast members).

Mulaney states he just had to text his sister, “Dad fell,” and voilà, she instantly appeared.

In a recent development, mikey Day plays a doctor who, as the author of the astutely named book Not It! A Son’s Guide to Elder Care, explains how it works.

“Years of internalized sexism warps Sister’s brain into thinking caretaking is her responsibility, and somehow, not yours,” Day claims. “Next, your text arrives, instantly activating her. And that’s it! You’re done for life! See you at the funeral!”.

Anyone who’s ever had to care for elderly parents can relate to Sister’s duties: Making those torturous, endless calls to doctors, insurance companies and pharmacists, all while screaming, “Speak to human!” at unhelpful phone trees.

A rapidly flashed line at the end of the ad notes, “Offer void if Sister has a good therapist,” who’d presumably tell her to insist her brothers do their share.

It wasn’t just a fictional sketch to some SNL viewers on Reddit.

“This isn’t funny, this is life for a lot of women,” wrote one person.

“We’re sharpening our focus on Roku’s core mission: being the top streaming platform,” a Roku spokesperson told Roettgers via email. “As part of that, we plan to wind down sales of smart home hardware and will provide continued support and services for Roku Smart Home products.”.

Roku was recently acquired by Fox, with the formal sale closing on Nov. 6.

Roku launched its own product lineup with proprietary hardware in 2025.

Roettgers remarked in his newsletter that, based on Roku’s own website, the number of products available for purchase appears to have dwindled. Right now, all but two of Roku’s smart home gear are listed as out of stock.

At other retailers like Home Depot, Amazon, and Walmart, many Roku listings have been removed or marked for clearance, while some retailers are only selling refurbished items.

It’s likely, as Roettgers identified in a previous newsletter, that Fox did not see long-term value in smart home gear for Roku, a fact certainly exacerbated by AI-induced hardware cost increases that have hit nearly every tech manufacturer, including Apple.

‘We need more reviewers’: Finding Linux bugs is easy now – fixing them is another story

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recently, Microsoft’s FORGE Lab reported that its AI scanning system, MDASH, turned up 59 upstream Linux kernel bug reports, including one flaw at least 21 years old.
  • Easy: in Linux, any bug can be a security bug.
  • Industry observers note that it’s not just Linux, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recently, Microsoft’s FORGE Lab reported that its AI scanning system, MDASH, turned up 59 upstream Linux kernel bug reports, including one flaw at least 21 years old. That’s less impressive than it sounds. For 2026, through Nov. 2, the Linux Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) team reported an average of 27 CVEs a day.

Why so many? Easy: in Linux, any bug can be a security bug. As Linux Torvalds told me in 2024, “Bugs will happen, and anything can be a security bug if somebody is clever enough to just figure out how to abuse it.” Besides, since Linux runs everything from smartphones to refrigerators to supercomputers, what may be a serious bug in one device may not even appear at all on another.

Industry observers note that it’s not just Linux, though. In the latest Windows Patch Tuesday security release, Microsoft reported 726 CVEs. The vast majority of these bug reports are coming from AI programmers. Finding bugs on anything is no longer the hard part. But reviewing and fixing them is, and both Microsoft developers and kernel maintainers are struggling to keep up.

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited.

As the FORGE Lab mentioned, “Finding bugs and fixing them are drastically out of balance.” Turning its findings into reports took more than four person-months because “human effort [is] the bottleneck.”.

Recent findings suggest that that’s hurting the overworked maintainers. On Nov. 10, an ARM engineer and Linux kernel maintainer Lorenzo Stoakes gave up reviewing code. He’d been a reviewer for the memory-management core, misc, reclaim, and Rust-related sections. Stoakes, a kernel contributor since 2014,  wrote, “Given the current throughput in the kernel resulting from AI-generated series, I unfortunately lack the bandwidth to generally be able to offer review except in those areas I maintain.”.

In a recent development, stoakes added, “Of course the AI wave has been horrible, and is getting significantly worse. At first it was once in a while that I’d see slop. Then it was at least once a week. Then every few days. Nowadays it’s pretty much half of what I see, if not more.”.

Also: Filing bugs for open-source apps is a huge help for devs – and easier than you think.

In a recent development, he’s not alone. As Greg Kroah-Hartman, the Linux kernel stable maintainer, said in a Q&A session at Open Source Summit Europe, “We don’t have enough people to review them, the onslaught of the LLM-generated patches. We need more reviewers. We don’t have enough. All of the maintainers are burnt out, and we have been for ten years.”.

It’s not all doom and gloom, though. Linux Torvalds, Linux’s creator, noted in a recent Linux Kernel Mailing List (LKML) message that much of the new code in the Linux 7.4 rc 2 “was driven by various AI fixes.”.

According to recent reports, he continued, “that on the bpf [Berkeley Packet Filter]- side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true. I think most other areas haven’t reached that point yet, but it’s at least a sign that we _may_ be starting to see the tide starting to turn. Don’t hold your breath, but maybe cross your fingers we’ll be getting there in the not entirely distant future.”.

We can but hope. In an interview, Kroah-Hartman isn’t so optimistic. “We are getting closer, yes, but not quite there yet.”  He’s not even willing to give a guesstimate of when human-approved AI fixes will catch up with and overcome AI bug reports.

Also: I locked down my OpenClaw agent with Claude Code – then dared it to escape.

In a recent development, daniel Steinberg, the creator of the open-source cURL project, is also cautiously optimistic. Steinberg, who’s been especially critical of AI slop bug reports, told me in an interview that he now believes “we manage the flood pretty well so far, even if it goes a little up and down in periods depending exactly on who sends us a new set of findings this particular week.”.

In a recent development, still, while AI bugs remain a major headache for now, AI bug fixes, along with the work of thousands of maintainers, may finally be starting to stem the AI bug flood. I still foresee long days and nights of work ahead.

Industry observers note that I also expect we’ll see more serious security breaches. In November alone, we saw a serious Linux TCP networking security hole revealed; the nasty Alpine Linux OpenSSH flaw; Alpine’s GitLab near-miss; and the wide-open PHP2Shell security problem, which many groups still haven’t patched.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, one major debate in investing right now, and a cause of concern for some economists, is the question: "Will the U.S.
  • Industry observers note that in the background of everyday life, Americans benefit from a unique privilege: Many countries around the world want to use and hold our currency.
  • According to recent reports, there's been some debate about whether this will continue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, one major debate in investing right now, and a cause of concern for some economists, is the question: "Will the U.S. dollar keep its status as the world's top reserve currency?" Many Americans who go about their daily business, like shopping for groceries or other household goods, might not think much about this. But it's important.

Industry observers note that in the background of everyday life, Americans benefit from a unique privilege: Many countries around the world want to use and hold our currency. The U.S. dollar is the most popular reserve currency for central banks and governments around the world. According to Federal Reserve data, as of 2024, 58.5% of total global foreign exchange reserves were held in U.S. dollars. The euro was in a distant second place, making up about 19%, followed by the Japanese yen at 5.6%.

According to recent reports, there's been some debate about whether this will continue. What if the U.S. dollar becomes less popular than other international currencies? What if America has a government debt crisis and investors flee American assets? What if the world loses confidence in America?

Jamie Dimon, the CEO of JPMorgan Chase (JPM -0.57%), made headlines for casting doubt upon those doubts. Dimon believes that the American dollar's status as the global reserve currency is not in danger -- as long as two key U.S. strengths stay in place.

If Dimon is correct, that could be good news for investors in U.S. dollar-denominated assets. Let's look at what the JPMorgan Chase CEO had to say, and why it matters for your investments.

Speaking at the Economic Club of Chicago last month, Dimon expressed confidence in the U.S. dollar and stated he doesn't believe it will lose its status as the world's most popular reserve currency. He said that the two most important factors in the U.S. dollar's dominance of foreign reserves are the U.S. military and the overall strength of the U.S. economy.

"If we have the strongest military in the world and the strongest economy in the world, we will be the preeminent reserve currency," Dimon noted.

Foreign governments and central banks tend to hold dollars because the dollar is widely used in international trade and is generally considered a safe, stable, and liquid asset. It's easy to move money with U.S. dollars or exchange U.S. Treasury bonds for cash. Not every country offers these advantages. The U.S. dollar's role as the No. 1 reserve currency also reflects America's strengths as a place to invest: a stable government, a strong economy, and the rule of law to protect investors' rights and freedoms.

Industry observers note that dimon's argument is that as long as America's economy leads the world and the U.S. military helps ensure global stability and protects international free trade, America will be a safe and desirable place for investors worldwide to put their money. That's good news for the U.S. dollar and investors in American stocks and bonds.

In a recent development, since so many banks, investors, and governments around the world trust the dollar and want to buy it, it creates demand that keeps the dollar’s value strong relative to other currencies. It also helps keep U.S. interest rates lower, enabling American consumers, businesses, and the U.S. government to keep borrowing money.

What if that all went away? A June 2026 research paper by Stanford University finance professors found that if the dollar lost its status as a foreign reserve currency, there would be adverse consequences. According to their model, the dollar would depreciate by 8.8%, the U.S. real interest rate would rise by about 0.9%, and there would be an aggregate loss of wealth of about one year of U.S. GDP (about $30.8 trillion, as of 2025).

According to recent reports, the good news is that it seems highly unlikely that the U.S. will lose its status as the world's favorite foreign currency -- at least not anytime soon, and not all at once. Other countries' currencies have some disadvantages that make them unlikely to replace the dollar.

Industry observers note that if you believe that the U.S. dollar will stay strong, you might want to keep investing in U.S. stocks, such as those in the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -0.04%). The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -0.15%) is a simple way to buy shares of the 500 largest publicly traded companies in America. If the U.S. economy performs well and the U.S. dollar remains strong, the companies in this S&P 500 ETF will likely benefit in the long term.

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (855 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Voyager 1 Will Be a Full Light-Day From Earth on Wednesday

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that NASA’s Voyager 1 left Earth on Sept.
  • According to recent reports, it’s quite an accomplishment for a spacecraft built in the mid-1970s One light-day is the distance that light travels in a single day at the speed of light, which is approximately 186,282 miles per second.
  • Sources indicate that fortunately, Voyager 1 has been traveling a bit faster than that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that NASA’s Voyager 1 left Earth on Sept. 5, 1977, carrying a camera, a set of science instruments and a gold-plated record of sounds and images from home. Forty-nine years later, it’s about to reach a distance no spacecraft has reached before: one light-day, or roughly 16.1 billion miles. At that range, light needs a full 24 hours to make the trip between Earth and the probe. NASA expects Voyager 1 to cross the line on Nov. 18, nearly five decades into a mission originally planned to last about five years.

According to recent reports, it’s quite an accomplishment for a spacecraft built in the mid-1970s One light-day is the distance that light travels in a single day at the speed of light, which is approximately 186,282 miles per second. That translates to 25.9 billion kilometers or about 16.1 billion miles in a single day. At an average human walking speed of 3 mph, it would take a human 612,015 years to walk that distance.

Sources indicate that fortunately, Voyager 1 has been traveling a bit faster than that. It presently zips along the cosmos at a steady 37,763 mph, a speed it achieved in 1980 after a gravity-assisted Saturn flyby. It has been flying at that speed ever since.

The milestone comes 14 years after its previous one, when Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause, the point where the sun’s heliosphere ends, and entered interstellar space. It’s also 28 years after passing Pioneer 10 to become the human-made object that has traveled the farthest into space.

Industry observers note that the historic milestone isn’t without its drama. Voyager 1 has been in space for nearly half a century, and in that time, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory has done everything it can to extend the life of Voyager 1. That includes troubleshooting issues, performing maintenance and shutting down various systems to save power and extend the spacecraft’s life-span.

According to recent reports, several of those efforts took place in 2026. The team running Voyager 1 spent weeks shutting down three devices and powering on three low-power alternatives to reduce overall power usage. This initiative, which was internally called The Big Bang, was also performed on Voyager 2. The transition was completed in early September, giving Voyager 1 more time with its dwindling power supply while also keeping it warm enough to continue operating in the frigid conditions of interstellar space.

It was a tricky maneuver that required the team to simultaneously turn multiple instruments on and off. The difficulty of the maneuver was amplified by the fact that it took almost a full day for any signal to reach Voyager and another full day for Voyager to send a signal back, with hours of downtime while the spacecraft performed the operations.

Industry observers note that all of this took place several months after Voyager 1 experienced a sudden drop in power, which necessitated shutting off one of its three remaining instruments still in operation. Voyager 1 now has only two instruments still in operation.

Industry observers note that making it a whole light-day away from Earth is likely going to be Voyager 1’s final milestone while it still has enough power to communicate with Earth. Voyager 1 is powered by three radioisotope thermoelectric generators. They are essentially nuclear-powered batteries that generate energy by converting the steady heat from decaying plutonium-238.

Recent findings suggest that when Voyager 1 first launched, its radioisotope thermoelectric generators produced about 470 watts of power. But plutonium-238 doesn’t last forever, and after 50 years in space, the RTGs now produce about 215 watts of power, with an average loss of about 4 watts per year. Most of that power is used to keep Voyager 1 up and running, which is why NASA has shut down eight of the 10 instruments that Voyager had when it launched.

At its current rate of usage and decay, Voyager 1 is expected to shut down its final science instrument in the 2030s and will eventually lose communication with Earth in 2036 due to insufficient power to send back a radio signal.

The same fate is expected for Voyager 2, Voyager 1’s twin, which has also spent half a century in space. While it is labeled the sequel, Voyager 2 actually debuted 16 days before Voyager 1, and the two have spent nearly identical amounts of time traversing the cosmos. Thanks to its slower speed and trajectory, it likely won’t reach the one light-day distance until after its instruments shut down.

According to recent reports, thanks to the vastness of space, Voyager 1 will lose all of its power before it hits its next milestone, which is the beginning of the Oort Cloud, a vast, icy shell of comets at the edge of our solar system. It’ll take about 300 years for Voyager 1 to make it there.

Thanks to the near-perfect vacuum of outer space, Voyager 1 will continue to fly at its current speed even after it shuts down entirely. So it’ll still hit that milestone; it just won’t be able to phone home to tell us about it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that like any AI, Google Gemini wants to remember things about you.
  • Also: I tried Claude Sheets on 3 tasks – and it saved me hours of work.
  • With a latest option called Memory summary, you’re able to view the details that Gemini has gathered about you over time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that like any AI, Google Gemini wants to remember things about you. The purported reason is to help tailor and personalize your conversations. But remember that your personal details may also wind up training the AI or even being reviewed by actual humans. With that in mind, you might want to find out just what Gemini knows about you. And now you can.

Also: I tried Claude Sheets on 3 tasks – and it saved me hours of work.

With a latest option called Memory summary, you’re able to view the details that Gemini has gathered about you over time. These may be tidbits from your conversations or things that you directly told the AI. Even better, you can add or remove any details just by editing the memory or issuing your request directly to Gemini.

This fresh capability is available in Gemini across the board, so you can access it at the Gemini website, in the mobile iOS and Android apps, and in the Windows and Mac desktop apps.

Sources indicate that launch Gemini via the web or in one of the mobile or desktop apps. In the left pane displaying your previous chats, select the Settings icon at the bottom. At the Settings screen, select Personal Intelligence and then click or tap Memory summary. If the option is grayed out, it means the Memory feature is turned off. To proceed, turn it back on. You can always turn if off again afterward if you wish.

You’ll then see the individual details by category. My summary arranged the information across such categories as Essentials, Business & Career, Reading & Interests, and Culinary Preferences. Go down the list to see the individual items in each category. To view a recent history, tap the three dot-icon at the top and select Memory history. This highlights you the latest changes and updates to Gemini’s memory.

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents.

What if Gemini’s memory includes details that are too personal or just incorrect? No problem. You can alter the AI’s memories of you. At the website or in one of the desktop apps, click the pencil icon at the top. Now you’re able to directly edit the text to add, remove, or revise specific details. After you’ve made your changes, just click Save.

For example, my summary said that I lived in Madison County. I have no idea where Gemini got that notion, as I live in New York. Here, I revised the text and saved the changes, which then synced across the Gemini website and apps.

The mobile apps have no direct editing capability. But there’s another method that works both on mobile and on the desktop. Just tell Gemini what change you want to make. At the prompt, type and speak your request, and the AI will carry it out for you.

Also: The best and worst AI for your privacy, ranked.

As an example, my summary stated that I run a business called Batter Up selling collectible baseball cards. That’s not at all true. I had once referred to such a store only to test Gemini’s image creation skills to design a logo for a baseball card seller. Here, I simply told Gemini that I don’t run a business called Batter Up and asked it to remove that item from its memory. Poof, that detail rapidly disappeared.

Google isn’t exactly known as being privacy-friendly, and that extends to Gemini. In this case, though, I give the manufacturer credit for offering this easy way to control the AI’s memories. I do find the memory feature useful as it recalls details about me that help personalize and direct its responses. But I don’t like Gemini or Google knowing too much about me. Now I can keep memory enabled and just control what it remembers about me.

Google Pixel Tag Hands-On: Android Fans Get Their Own AirTag-Style Tracker

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1267 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if a firm releases a product in an already established market, is it worth the effort?
  • In a recent development, the Pixel Tag is available now for $30 each or $100 in a pack of four.
  • Industry observers note that it isn’t the first Android-compatible tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if a firm releases a product in an already established market, is it worth the effort? If you think I’m talking about Apple and Google, you’d be right – but this isn’t the iPhone Duo muscling into the folding phone fray. This time, the roles are reversed: Google has released the Pixel Tag, a small Bluetooth tracker that it hopes will be the Android ecosystem’s answer to Apple’s near-ubiquitous AirTag.

In a recent development, the Pixel Tag is available now for $30 each or $100 in a pack of four. It works with Android phones and uses Google’s Find Hub technology for tracking over distances beyond Bluetooth range. If you use an Android phone and have wanted the capability to track things such as keys, bags, bikes, vehicles and other indispensable items, and you want the tech to come from the firm that designed the system, the Pixel Tag is an excellent choice.

Industry observers note that it isn’t the first Android-compatible tracker. Motorola introduced its Moto Tag 2 earlier this year, and Tile has been the de facto AirTag alternative for several years. There’s also now a growing ecosystem of other items that tap into Apple’s Find My and Android’s Find Hub networks, ranging from slim credit-card-sized devices like the Rolling Square AirCard Pro and Peak Design’s Beacon Finder Card, to novel approaches like Falcam’s TagBatt, a battery for some Sony and Canon mirrorless cameras that integrates Apple Find My tracking.

In a recent development, google jumping into this more crowded field tells me the manufacturer thinks there’s profit to be made by manufacturing its own hardware and software. It’s also investing in the infrastructure it’s already built out, and not leaving the hardware side to a constellation of other vendors.

Recent findings suggest that trackers like the Pixel Tag and AirTag can be a surprisingly deflating purchase: You pair them with your phone, put them into something you don’t want to lose track of – then forget about them. They’re usually not tactile the way a phone, watch or laptop is each day. And their value doesn’t kick into action until you think an item has gone missing.

After slinging AirTags into bags and dangling them off keychains, one thing I really appreciate about the Pixel Tag is its thinness. Apple chose a small, round footprint, even keeping the exact design for the second-generation AirTags. Google instead opted for a longer lozenge shape, at 1.8 inches (46.1mm), that is about two-thirds the height of the AirTag at 0.2 inch (5.4mm).

Recent findings suggest that google sent a Bellroy leather keychain as a sample accessory for review, and paired with the Pixel Tag, the two are a fine size for a pocket or clipped to an inside bag pocket. I thought the longer design would get in the way, but it’s not bad at all.

Sources indicate that the Pixel Tag uses a CR2032 coin-sized battery that should last about a year (the same as the AirTag). It also has an IP67 rating, which is durable in 1 meter of water for up to 30 minutes.

Another departure from the AirTag is a physical button, making the Pixel Tag even more tactile. When you’re using Find Hub on your phone to locate it by sound, press once to stop the chirps it makes. Or, if you have the tag in hand (on a keychain, for example) and need to find your phone, press twice to ring the phone – it makes a pleasant sing-songy chime that gets louder and more intense as it continues, so I’m confident it’ll be easy to locate, even among couch cushions.

Industry observers note that speaking of the chimes, credit to the Google sound designers who came up with the Pixel Tag’s tune. It has three levels of loudness you can set, and seems plenty audible enough when you’re spelunking the living room for it. I measured it at 80 decibels, which when compared to the second-generation AirTag volume, is 7 less than the 87 decibels of Apple’s tracker.

One more nice touch compared to the AirTag: the Find Hub app shows the tag’s battery status. If that gets to Low or Very Low, the app sends you notifications every two weeks until the battery is replaced. After Apple showed battery statuses on AirTags in early versions of the Find My app, the organization changed the Find My app so it only indicates battery when it’s low and needs to be replaced.

Recent findings suggest that the best feature of either tracker is the ability to locate its exact location – not which building or room it’s in, but to tell if the item fell behind the couch or was accidentally dropped in the driveway. (Yes, I’m making up these examples from personal experience.).

In a recent development, precision Finding uses a combination of Bluetooth 6.0 (via a feature called Channel Sounding) and the ultra-wideband chips inside the tag and the phone to directionally find the tracker when it’s within Bluetooth range. You hold the phone upright, perpendicular to the ground for the best connection. Then you wander your space, watching the indicator change as you get closer to the tag.

According to recent reports, on the Pixel Tag, that indication is a wobbly circle shape that fills in as you get closer; when you’re on top of the tracker, the shape is fully filled. The Find Hub app also uses the camera and UWB chip to include an estimated distance in feet and inches (or meters and centimeters). When you’re close enough, the tracking shape becomes a directional arrow to point you the right way. UWB is compatible with the Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8 Fold and newer Pixel phones.

Sources indicate that in my testing, the Find Nearby feature performed fairly well. Find Hub using a Pixel 11 Pro XL connected from within about 25 feet, including on multiple levels of a house when I was above or below it.

Sources indicate that perhaps because I was raised on science-fiction devices like the trackers in Aliens, though, I expected more consistent readings. There were times when both I and the tag remained stationary. The distance estimates would fluctuate by several feet.

Since I’ve had this review unit for only a few days, I haven’t yet had a chance to send it off with someone else and see if I can track it remotely using the Find Hub network. When nearby Android devices detect the Pixel Tag’s presence, they should securely and privately relay the tracker’s location to Google’s servers. (Apple’s Find My network operates the same way.) I’ll upgrade this article once I’ve taken the tag on such an adventure.

Sources indicate that tracking all your stuff is invaluable – I learned this first-hand earlier this year when I left a small bag containing my passport in a hotel room, and was able to convince the hotel that the bag was still on the premises. But unfortunately, smart tags are being used to track people without their knowledge.

Industry observers note that google is taking the same approach as Apple to help thwart this type of tracking. If a tag is separated from the phone it’s paired with (or the phone of someone else you’ve chosen to share the tag location with), and the tag is moved, its chime activates.

The idea is that you’ll hear an unfamiliar chirp and investigate. It has an NFC chip that displays its information when you tap it using the NFC built into a phone.

Latest Update: AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The best AI models on the market couldn’t find zero-days earlier this year, but now they can in less than 15 minutes and at a cost of a few bucks, according to a new report from penetration testing firm Xint.io.
  • According to recent reports, every major AI developer is working at breakneck speed to improve model effectiveness.
  • This is good news for businesses trying to harness AI for productivity and newly introduced services, but as token prices fall, it has also become cheaper for attackers to launch AI-assisted attacks, including software breaches caused by exploiting unknown vulnerabilities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The best AI models on the market couldn’t find zero-days earlier this year, but now they can in less than 15 minutes and at a cost of a few bucks, according to a new report from penetration testing firm Xint.io. The findings raise questions about how vulnerabilities will be discovered and exploited in the future.

According to recent reports, every major AI developer is working at breakneck speed to improve model effectiveness. At the same time, token prices continue to fall, with studies showing that the average cost of tokens, which varies by domain, has dropped by about 47% per quarter since 2023 and 15% last month alone, due to intense competition among companies including OpenAI and Anthropic.

This is good news for businesses trying to harness AI for productivity and newly introduced services, but as token prices fall, it has also become cheaper for attackers to launch AI-assisted attacks, including software breaches caused by exploiting unknown vulnerabilities.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

A report published by Xint.io examines how popular AI models have evolved over the past year to the point where cybersecurity tasks that would have failed only months ago now succeed. The team analyzed seven models launched since February 2026: two from OpenAI, three from Anthropic, and two open-source models from DeepSeek and Z.ai. The team tracked, over time, how they performed in finding a target vulnerability.

The target of this research was a security flaw in Google’s V8 engine. Tracked as CVE-2026-102321, the type confusion bug leading to remote code execution (RCE) was disclosed to the Google Vulnerability Reward Program (VRP) by Xint researcher Taisic Yun and so was not present in the AI models’ training datasets.

The research scope was limited to a set of source files, including the file containing the vulnerability, and each model was instructed to search for security issues within these files.

Xint’s first test was conducted in February. After 25 hours and $350 of scanning, the best models then available still couldn’t find the critical vulnerability.

In July, GPT 5.6 Sol found the zero-day flaw for $22 in 44 minutes.

Also: Finding Linux bugs is easy – fixing them is another story.

By September, GPT 6 Sol discovered the bug in 13 minutes for only $4.24 with its first guided prompt.

Only three of the seven models found the bug: GPT 6 Sol, GPT 5.6 Sol, and Claude Opus 5, all debuted from July onward. GPT 5.6 Sol needed two prompts, while Claude Opus 5 found it on its first try but at a higher cost of $43.40.

DeepSeek’s and Z.ai’s models failed the task.

The researchers say that the combination of AI model development and low token prices means that “mediocre hackers” can now use frontier models effectively to discover and potentially exploit vulnerabilities, and “while we are still far from complete amateurs using unharnessed models to hack systems and applications, what used to be considered too hard and costly to be worth the effort of the average hacker is now reachable.”.

As a result, organizations need to adjust their security posture accordingly — but falling token costs and evolving AI skills and speed can also work in your favor.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

There’s nothing stopping an organization’s security team or pentesters from running the same checks themselves to find vulnerabilities before threat actors do. AI-assisted tests, arguably, are no longer something that can be pushed back to next year’s budgetary review. By performing a risk assessment that focuses on likely weak spots, such as public-facing services or a digital supply chain that hasn’t been audited for years, organizations can mitigate the risk AI-enabled cyberattacks pose.

Sources indicate that zero-day vulnerabilities are unknown to vendors, and a patch might not be available when they go public or are actively exploited in the wild. So, AI can only go so far, but it can free up your defenders for tasks that need the human touch. Furthermore, maintaining zero-trust access controls, segmenting and shoring up your network’s defenses, and monitoring endpoints for signs of suspicious behavior can do as much as, or more than, AI.

In a recent development, as Xint notes, “expertise still matters” when it comes to instructing AI models to discover vulnerabilities. In some cases, the models couldn’t find the target vulnerability without guidance, so additional runs were needed, increasing time and cost.

“Software breaches still require some level of technical proficiency,” the researchers say, “but no longer top-of-the-distribution expertise.”.

The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
  • The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
  • "The size of the Treasury purchases confirmed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases confirmed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

According to recent reports, gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

Bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

In a recent development, the Treasury Department noted last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the prepares.

Recent findings suggest that last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

It has been revealed that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

It has been revealed that "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold mentioned in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah stated. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

In a recent development, the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah mentioned. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

In a recent development, "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Industry observers note that coltman at 21Shares remarked the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh noted in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder noted.

"The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (968 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Five iOS 27 Toggles That Make Your iPhone Easier to Read and More Private

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (968 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo ship with iOS 27’s default settings, and so does any older iPhone that updated this fall.
  • They’re easy to change once you know where to look.
  • Read more: Win a Latest Apple Watch in CNET Big Guessing Game Contest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo ship with iOS 27’s default settings, and so does any older iPhone that updated this fall. Those defaults include a strong Liquid Glass effect, automatic subtitles on videos and a Siri that saves and syncs your conversations.

They’re easy to change once you know where to look. Here are five settings worth adjusting, whether you’re setting up a upcoming phone or finally getting around to it on your current one.

Read more: Win a Latest Apple Watch in CNET Big Guessing Game Contest.

Sources indicate that apple introduced Liquid Glass with iOS 26, giving menus, buttons, notifications and other interface elements a translucent appearance. Not everyone was a fan of the upcoming design, and with iOS 27, you now get more control over exactly how transparent the interface looks.

Go to Settings > Appearance > Liquid Glass. Drag the slider to the right to add more tint and opacity, making buttons and text easier to distinguish from whatever is behind them. Moving it left makes the interface more transparent.

If the most opaque setting still isn’t enough, go to Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size and turn on Reduce Transparency. This makes translucent backgrounds more solid across iOS, although it overrides the regular Liquid Glass appearance controls.

More tint makes Liquid Glass easier to read.

It has been revealed that the new Siri AI works similarly t ChatGPT or Claude in iOS 27. It now comes complete with a dedicated app where you can revisit previous conversations. Those chats sync through iCloud so you can start a conversation on your iPhone and continue it on another Apple device, such as your Mac.

By default, iOS 27 keeps those conversations forever, but there is a way to automatically get rid of older conversations if you don’t want them piling up.

If you don’t need a permanent archive of everything you ask Siri, go to Settings > Siri > Keep Conversations and choose 30 Days or 1 Year. Selecting either option permanently deletes conversations beyond that timeframe.

Siri keeps your conversations forever unless you choose a shorter limit.

While you’re there, tap Opens To and select A Upcoming Conversation if you want the Siri app to open with a blank chat instead of showing your recent conversations every time.

Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or 15 Pro Max, iPhone Air or an iPhone 16 or later.

iOS 27 puts a fresh Write with Siri button above the keyboard in apps including Messages, Mail and Notes. You can ask Siri AI to draft something from scratch, proofread what you’ve written or rewrite it in a different tone.

The thing is, I’m not a significant fan of the AI writing tools, so I don’t use them at all.

Industry observers note that if you prefer writing without the extra AI prompt like I do, you can restrict Siri’s writing features by using Screen Time. Go to Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions, turn on the restriction and then tap Siri > Writing Assistance > Don’t Allow.

Screen Time lets you completely disable Siri’s writing tools.

This disables access to the writing tools across your iPhone, rather than simply hiding the keyboard button, so only do this if you don’t use Apple’s AI writing tools at all. You can return to the same menu and choose Allow if you want them back. Apple documents the restriction under its Apple Intelligence Screen Time controls.

Introduced back in iOS 17, Siri can now wake up when you simply say “Siri” instead of “Hey Siri.” The one-word command is convenient, but it also makes accidental activations more likely whenever someone notes Siri’s name in a conversation or a video they’re watching online.

Siri goes absolutely bonkers whenever I’m in work meetings about Apple features.

To disable the feature, go to Settings > Siri > Talk to Siri. Choose “Hey Siri” instead of “Siri.”.

Requiring “Hey Siri” can help prevent accidental activations.

You’ll still be able to bring up Siri with your voice, but the extra word makes it less likely to wake up when you aren’t talking to it directly.

This isn’t exclusive to iOS 27, but it’s been annoying me more recently, so thought I would throw it in here, especially with Siri AI being the prominent feature on this enhancement.

Sources indicate that iOS 27 now automatically highlights subtitles on videos in Photos, Safari and other apps that use Apple’s video player. I don’t mind captions when I need them, but they can take up too much of the video and distract me from whatever I’m watching.

They don’t appear randomly though. By default, iOS can turn them on when the video is in another language, when your iPhone is muted or when you skip back.

Whenever subtitles appear in Apple’s video player, you can tap the video to show the playback controls, tap the More Controls button, select Subtitles and choose Off.

You can disable subtitles per video.

According to recent reports, if iOS keeps turning them on because it thinks the video is in another language, go to Settings > Accessibility > Subtitles & Captioning. Under Automatic Subtitles, turn off When Languages Don’t Match.

The same menu also has switches for Show When Muted and Show on Skip Back, so you can disable those behaviors individually without turning off every automatic subtitle feature.

You can also disable each automatic subtitle trigger individually.

Some apps and websites use their own video players, so you may need to find a separate CC or subtitles button instead.

For more on iOS 27, check out this article on the features it brings to your iPhone and how Siri AI helped one of my colleagues avoid eating diarrhea lettuce.

#16023. Latest Update: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (844 w)
📖 Baca
