    #15990. 5 Brokerage Features We’re Excited for in 2027 (And 2 Things We Could Do Without)

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2309 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    5 Brokerage Features We’re Excited for in 2027 (And 2 Things We Could Do Without)

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2309 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Each fall, our investing team spends the latter half of the year hands-on testing a wide range of brokers, from legacy firms like Charles Schwab and Fidelity to newer, mobile-first firms like Public and M1.
    • According to recent reports, this year, we opened or tested more than 15 brokerage accounts, funded them and placed real trades.
    • While our updated reviews and final star ratings are still in the works, here is a preview of five things that really stood out to us this season — and two things we’re feeling a bit wary of.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Each fall, our investing team spends the latter half of the year hands-on testing a wide range of brokers, from legacy firms like Charles Schwab and Fidelity to newer, mobile-first firms like Public and M1.

    According to recent reports, this year, we opened or tested more than 15 brokerage accounts, funded them and placed real trades. We sent each broker a detailed questionnaire covering more than 65 data points and then verified, categorized and scored their responses using our proprietary scoring system. And finally, though our team is spread across the U.S., we met in person to compare the experience of using each platform.

    While our updated reviews and final star ratings are still in the works, here is a preview of five things that really stood out to us this season — and two things we’re feeling a bit wary of.

    Setting up buy and sell orders can be a pain point for some investors, especially beginners. Until recently, every platform required you to type in the ticker symbol, choose between dollars and shares, punch in the numbers and choose your order type. This creates opportunities for mistakes.

    Recent findings suggest that in recent months, AI has stepped in to help. Many platforms have released agents that you can ask to set up trades for you using natural language. Beginners aren’t the only people who benefit; some trading agents can also set up automated strategies based on prompts, thereby saving advanced traders a lot of time and effort monitoring the markets.

    Public’s “Agents” feature, which started rolling out in March and became available to all customers in August, has become a trailblazer in agentic trading. It can place trades for you, set up recurring trades to automate a strategy (Managing Editor Chris Davis experimented with a “buy the open, sell the close” strategy for a while), and even sweep uninvested cash into one of Public’s high-yield cash management account options.

    It has been revealed that robinhood also waded into the agentic trading space in early 2025 with the launch of its Cortex assistant, whose early iterations could place individual trades for you. In September of this year, the broker began rolling out Robinhood Agents, a more sophisticated natural-language interface that can build automated strategies based on a prompt, similar to Public’s Agents.

    Interactive Brokers also offers a simple AI agent (IBot) that can set up trades for you, as does Cash App (Moneybot), but these are limited to one-time actions and cannot automate more complex strategies. Still, they can simplify the trading experience for beginners. That might be especially valuable to Cash App users, given the platform’s “My First Brokerage” ethos.

    — Samuel Taube, Lead Investing Writer.

    » Curious about trading with a text prompt? Compare brokers with AI trading tools.

    There’s been another profound shift in the past year that involves AI: agents that can actually help you manage your brokerage account. So far, some of the newer, mobile-first platforms seem to have an edge over the long-established financial behemoths. It’s also a mind-bending gray area: If an AI is giving you portfolio advice, who’s accountable for the advice it gives? Can you trust it? And how is it any different from a robo-advisor?

    In our reviews this year, we looked into these questions. But here's a quick look at how one platform in particular is approaching this newly introduced frontier.

    According to recent reports, from my testing over the years, I was already a huge fan of M1’s portfolio-building system, and now that it's integrated an AI advisor into the app (to be specific, M1 bills it as an SEC-registered AI fiduciary investment advisor legally required to act in your best interest), M1 has created what I truly think is a one-of-a-kind product and service. I checked the forms M1 is required to submit to the SEC, and the organization declares outright that the AI advisor looks at your entire financial situation and gives actionable recommendations. In my experience with the app, those recommendations are based on your balances, the knowledge you provide and the ongoing conversations you have. There’s a lot to discuss here, which we’ll cover in our full M1 review, but suffice it to say, this is very impressive.

    Most brokers don’t charge many fees these days. Trading, inactivity and account fees have slowly but surely disappeared, making investing more affordable over the years. But there is one fee you still have to pay: an expense ratio.

    Most of the time, brokers have little control over expense ratios, since they’re set by fund managers. The only way a broker could offer an index fund without an expense ratio is if it was substantial enough to eat the cost.

    Industry observers note that this is exactly what Fidelity did back in 2018, when they introduced their “ZERO” funds. These funds have no expense ratios and no minimums, meaning they’re totally free for investors.

    Recent findings suggest that fidelity remained the only broker to offer this kind of fund until 2025, when E*TRADE introduced a very similar lineup of no-expense-ratio index funds. The suite of funds from both brokers is fairly broad — think large-cap, total market, international — which makes them especially attractive to beginners building a portfolio from scratch.

    Industry observers note that now, you may be wondering why these brokers decided to stray from the industry standard and offer products that don’t make them money. The idea is that the free funds will get you in the door — since you can only buy them if you have an account with that particular broker — and you’ll spend money on some other product they offer.

    Sources indicate that but does that make free index funds any less great? No. I still think it’s a massive step toward making investing more accessible for everyone, and I’m excited to see which brokers might add a similar offering in the future.

    — Bella Avila, Investing Editor.

    » Take a closer look: Compare Fidelity's and E*TRADE's free index funds.

    I'm a massive believer in putting every dollar to work, but that goal can sometimes fall through the cracks. Idle cash sitting uninvested in your brokerage account is a common oversight. It can easily pile up if you forget to reinvest sale proceeds or dividends (something I do more often than I’d like to admit). Or maybe you leave it parked for too long in your brokerage’s default account while waiting on a good investment opportunity.

    Sources indicate that thankfully, most brokerages offer some form of interest on that uninvested money. Some put the idle funds in a money market fund, which can offer yields that mirror market rates. Others “sweep” your unused cash into partner banks to take advantage of FDIC insurance.

    In today’s environment, people with money in savings vehicles like high-yield savings accounts or new CDs are well-positioned to take advantage of high rates. What sets some brokerages apart is whether they operate similarly. That is, do they raise rates in response to larger economic circumstances? And if so, how swiftly?

    Sources indicate that robinhood and Public are two firms on our radar that are offering competitive rates in response to hikes, ranging from 3.6% to 3.75% as of this writing. Robinhood requires a premium subscription to unlock those higher rates, while Public’s already high base rate of 3.3% applies to all customers and can be boosted to 3.75% with a Reserve membership. For investors who keep a lot of cash in their account, the extra fee can be worth it.

    Interest rates, of course, shouldn’t be the main reason you pick one broker over another. Costs, the types of securities available and platform usability are better starting points. But when a company meets those expectations and also offers a compelling interest rate on your uninvested money, it’s worth taking a closer look.

    — Sabrina Parys, Investing Editor.

    » See which brokers pay the most on idle cash: Best brokerages for high interest rates.

    Industry observers note that direct indexing is a strategy in which you replicate an existing stock index (like the S&P 500, for example) but customize it how you like. The most popular reason people choose direct indexing is for tax optimization — but it’s not the only one.

    Sources indicate that direct indexing can also be used to avoid overexposure to a specific tech giant. For instance, if you work at Apple and get company stock, you probably don’t need even more exposure to Apple through the S&P 500. Direct indexing lets you replace that one stock with a similar company instead.

    And then there’s the reason direct indexing appealed to me: it lets you avoid buying into companies you just don’t support. I’m sure we all invest in companies we don’t necessarily mesh with morally, but direct indexing can help you avoid that.

    It has been revealed that the strategy used to be available only to people with an advisor managing their investment account, and they had to have millions to get started. More recently, these minimums have dropped. And now, it’s not just for people with financial advisors — online brokers offer the strategy, too.

    Industry observers note that while some brokers still have steep minimums of $100,000 or so, others let you get started with less. Fidelity, in true Fidelity fashion, started offering direct indexing to clients a few years ago through a managed portfolio that has a minimum investment requirement of only $5,000.

    I was pleased to see Public launch direct indexing with a minimum of only $1,000 a year ago. However, we should note that with a low investment amount, you can only track a portion of an index.

    It has been revealed that but even with those limitations, I think it’s great that these companies are putting out the message that there shouldn’t be a huge barrier to entry to customize your portfolio. As direct indexing continues to gain popularity, we’ll be watching whether more brokers start offering it, as advancements in AI undoubtedly make it easier to do so.

    — Bella Avila, Investing Editor.

    It’s hard to ignore the rise of prediction markets in the mainstream. These days, it takes just a few clicks to bet on who might win the Super Bowl or take home a Grammy. These markets, which operate on contracts with binary outcomes, are easy to access and use everyday language, making them all the more tempting to try — and now they are beginning to appear on many broker platforms and apps.

    Sources indicate that we’d like to be clear on this one: Our editors have no intention of telling you how to spend your extra discretionary money. If you have a solid financial foundation and have allocated a few bucks to bet on some event contracts, that’s all good. But as editors who view investing apps as vehicles for legitimate wealth-building strategies, we draw the line at these products being marketed alongside other investments, such as stocks, ETFs and mutual funds.

    In fact, this year we’ve actually decided to dock points in our annual reviews and ratings from brokerages that offer unrestricted access to event and sports-style prediction markets. In our view, these products aren’t conducive to long-term investing, and they’re speculative without enough oversight — a troublesome combination. You can read more about our stance and why we’re taking it here.

    — Sabrina Parys, Investing Editor.

    I’d venture to say that since the dawn of social media, people have been talking about investing online. And nowadays, the online investing community is huge. The r/investing subreddit has more than 3.5 million followers, and even on a video-forward platform like TikTok, #investing has 4.1 million posts under it.

    But is where people go to talk about investing online changing?

    The first broker I saw incorporate a social media–style element into its platforms was etoro. When you scroll down on the app's “home” tab, you’re met with what looks like an X feed. And the CopyTrader feature lets you copy another person’s portfolio, with that section of the app highlighting “trending investors,” “market outperformers,” and more.

    Industry observers note that this wasn’t a huge surprise to me coming from a niche broker with presumably a large user base of active traders. What surprised me was when Robinhood added a social media-style section to its app, testing a beta version in March and expanding it to all U.S. users in October.

    Robinhood Social is, again, much like an X feed but for showing people which stocks you’re buying or selling. When I created an account to see what it was all about, the app encouraged me to share my “stats” on my profile (my one-day and one-year profit and loss, and my profit rate). “Trading stats build trust and transparency on Social,” the app remarked.

    You could argue that other, even bigger brokers promote social trading. Fidelity, for example, has a “customer orders” section that indicates how many Fidelity customers are buying and selling certain stocks (though, I’ll say, they don’t promote this feature and it’s buried in the app).

    It has been revealed that the huge difference, in my opinion, is that Fidelity leaves it up to you to research these stocks. There’s no feed or comment section. On etoro and Robinhood, people can say whatever they want about why they bought or sold a certain security — whether truthful or not — or worse, why you should or shouldn’t invest in something.

    Sources indicate that to me, the whole concept of social trading feels like the antithesis of long-term investing. It’s a trend that I hope we don’t see becoming more popular among big-name brokers.

    — Bella Avila, Investing Editor.

    Disclosure: Neither the authors nor the editor owned any of the aforementioned investments at the time of publication.

    Global stock markets have been volatile as investors assess high bond yields and continued tensions between the U.S. and Iran. There are concerns about the impact of uncertainty in the Middle East on oil prices and consequently on inflation.

    Investors who prefer to look beyond short-term noise and buy stocks with attractive long-term growth potential can follow the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts. The ratings of these experts are backed by in-depth research of a manufacturer's financials and thorough analysis of the factors affecting its business performance.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Semiconductor giant Nvidia (NVDA) reported stellar fiscal second-quarter results and reassured investors about continued strength in AI-driven demand for its chips. Moreover, Nvidia's FY28 revenue growth outlook of 70% was well above the Street's expectations.

    Industry observers note that reacting to the Q2 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore reiterated a buy rating on NVDA and increased his price target to $300 from $288. "This is our Top Pick in the semis group, with a compelling product cycle, exceptional growth and valuation below peers," said the 5-star analyst.

    Nvidia delivered impressive quarterly results despite supply constraints, Moore said, but he believes that the FY28 revenue and gross margin commentary mattered more, with a favorable outlook for both measures.

    According to recent reports, moore remarked Nvidia's 70% revenue growth guidance for FY28 was above his own estimate of 52% and the consensus of about 40%. The top-line growth estimate was a "remarkable figure" given supply concerns and Moore said he expects Nvidia to continue to address bottlenecks to deliver rapid growth.

    Among other takeaways, the analyst stated performance metrics for Vera Rubin chips were strong, with Nvidia emphasizing a 30x higher throughput per megawatt and 35x lower token cost compared with Grace Blackwell Ultra.

    Moore ranks No. 159 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 60% of the time, delivering an average return of 24.60%. See Nvidia Statistics on TipRanks.

    Ride-hailing and delivery platform Uber Technologies (UBER) was recommended by BMO Capital analyst Brian Pitz, who discussed the firm's opportunity in the autonomous vehicle (AV) market in a recent research note that reiterated a buy rating and price target of $119.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted Uber's transition into a diversified marketplace, with investors now focusing on its AV growth prospects. The key question is how much value can Uber generate as AVs become commercialized, Pitz asked.

    "We continue to believe that Uber's AV strategy is evolving and will become a significant driver of revenue and profitability," the analyst stated.

    Importantly, Pitz believes that Uber can establish itself as a preferred mobility platform for AV makers, supported by its growing AV infrastructure capabilities and an expanding partner base. This would enable Uber to win a significant share of value as the AV market is commercialized.

    Additionally, Pitz noted Uber's enhanced position in the AV value chain, with the company shifting from serving as a distribution channel for robotaxis to becoming a broader platform for AV mobility. The analyst discussed Uber's efforts to capture growth opportunities in the AV market, including higher capital spending, expansion into new markets and building partnerships beyond Alphabet's Waymo.

    Recent findings suggest that pitz ranks No. 574 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of about 12.20%. See Uber Technologies Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Semiconductor organization Marvell Technology (MRVL) recently declared better-than-expected results for the second quarter of FY27. But the company's increased FY28 guidance fell short of investors' high expectations.

    In reaction to the Q2 FY27 results, KeyBanc analyst John Vinh reaffirmed a buy rating on Marvell Technology, with a price target of $400. The analyst noted that Marvell's results and outlook were driven by strength in its data center business. The Q2 FY27 data center business grew 46% year-over-year, to $2.17 billion, far above KeyBanc's estimate of $2.09 billion.

    Management "highlighted accelerating AI networking demand across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up architectures, supported by strong 800G optical DSP demand, rapid 1.6T ramp, broader 51.2T switch deployments and higher TIA/driver demand," Vinh said.

    Consequently, Marvell raised its data center revenue guidance, now expecting 60% growth in FY27 and more than 60% in FY28.

    Recent findings suggest that regarding the recently confirmed $120 billion warrant arrangement with Google, Vinh said management argued that programs tied to the warrant are already priced into the custom outlook through FY28. Meanwhile, new programs and those in execution are expected to drive significant upside to the previous FY29 custom XPU revenue estimate of over $10 billion, Vinh said, citing management.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that when you build a retirement plan around ending your career at a certain age, and you're forced to exit the labor force sooner, it can constitute a pretty big blow.
    • Recent findings suggest that the good news is that being pushed out of the workforce ahead of schedule doesn't have to completely upend your long-term plans.
    • In a recent development, if you're forced into early retirement due to a layoff, the first thing to do is review your exit package.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that when you build a retirement plan around ending your career at a certain age, and you're forced to exit the labor force sooner, it can constitute a pretty big blow. But it's not totally uncommon to be forced into an earlier retirement due to a layoff, health challenges, or the need to care for a loved one.

    Recent findings suggest that the good news is that being pushed out of the workforce ahead of schedule doesn't have to completely upend your long-term plans. Here's how to pivot and salvage the situation.

    In a recent development, if you're forced into early retirement due to a layoff, the first thing to do is review your exit package. You may be entitled to severance pay, plus compensation for accrued vacation and/or sick time.

    Take the time to review the details of your severance agreement so you know what to expect. Also keep in mind that your agreement may include certain restrictions, so don't just gloss over the fine print.

    It has been revealed that being forced into retirement sooner than planned could mean losing your health insurance. If you're not yet 65, you're typically too young for Medicare, which means you'll need to secure coverage on your own.

    Take the time to review your options, which may include COBRA if you can afford the premiums or an Affordable Care Act marketplace proposal. If your spouse is still working and has insurance through their job, joining that health plan may be the most affordable bet. While you should make sure to compare your choices thoroughly, don't wait, because going without health insurance is inherently risky.

    It has been revealed that if you're at least 62 when you're forced to retire, it means you're old enough to start collecting Social Security. Whether you should start benefits is a different question.

    You won't get your Social Security benefits in full until age 67 if you were born in 1960 or later. And for each year you delay your claim past that point, until age 70, your benefits get a permanent 8% boost.

    Filing for Social Security ahead of schedule could reduce a critical income stream for life, so before you do that, assess your retirement savings. You may be able to comfortably withdraw additional money from your IRA or 401(k) for a period of time so you can hold off on taking benefits right away.

    Industry observers note that retiring sooner than planned could mean that your savings have to last longer, and that you need to reduce portfolio risk sooner. Take the time to assess your portfolio and make sure you have at least a few years' worth of safe investments, like bonds.

    Sources indicate that it's also wise to set yourself up with enough cash to cover one to two years of expenses. That way, if you need money when your portfolio is down, you won't have to lock in permanent losses by liquidating assets at a bad time.

    If the reason for your forced retirement boils down to being downsized out of a job and you can't find a new one in your field, it doesn't mean your days of working have to end. You may be able to find flexible part-time work that lets you earn some income and stay busy.

    Let's say you were earning $8,000 a month at your full-time job. If you're able to find gig work or a part-time role that lets you earn $2,000 a month, you're looking at a $6,000 monthly income shortfall instead of $8,000. Those part-time wages could take some pressure off your savings if you're tapping your IRA or 401(k) sooner than planned.

    Industry observers note that just as importantly, having a job to go to could be good for your mental health. Even if you don't necessarily need the money, it could be an option worth pursuing.

    Being forced to end your career before you're ready is not an easy situation to cope with. Taking the steps above could help protect your finances as you navigate your latest reality.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -0.45%) have soared impressively over the past five years, rising by an incredible 244% during this period. However, it is worth noting that the majority of the stock's gains have arrived over the past 18 months.

    The stock has simply taken off since May 2025, jumping by 421% and crushing the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite index's 38% gains over the same period. The good news for investors is that AMD stock can deliver substantial gains over the next five years, even after its red-hot rally.

    Let's check out AMD's prospects and see where the stock could be after five years.

    AMD is gradually becoming a key player in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market, as evident from the manufacturer's third-quarter results. Its data center revenue increased by 97% from the year-ago period to a record $8.5 billion. The company is benefiting from the phenomenal demand for its Instinct data center graphics cards and Epyc server processors.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:51 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Additionally, AMD has started shipping its Helios rack-scale server solutions to customers. It expects Helios shipments to increase substantially going forward, driven by increased production by AMD's partners. Not surprisingly, AMD expects stronger data center revenue growth in 2027. The firm previously expected data center revenue to more than double next year but now expects "data center AI revenue to grow even faster than we projected 90 days ago.".

    AMD can sustain healthy data center revenue growth over the next five years considering that capital spending on AI infrastructure could increase from $765 billion in 2026 to $1.64 trillion in 2031. AI chips alone could generate over $1.1 trillion in revenue in 2031, up from $494 billion this year. As AMD gains a larger share of the AI chip market, it will be able to capture a larger share of this lucrative addressable opportunity.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, Microsoft and Sony could launch their next-generation gaming consoles in late 2028. AMD is designing the semi-custom processors that power these consoles, which means its gaming segment is likely to step on the gas once again. AMD reported a 40% year-over-year decline in gaming revenue in Q3 to $773 million, citing lower sales of semi-custom processors due to the age of the current console cycle.

    However, the ramp-up of a new console cycle has historically been a tailwind for AMD, and the trend could continue as consumers upgrade to new consoles in the next five years.

    AMD's earnings per share (EPS) are anticipated to increase by 94% in 2026 to $8.08. The next couple of years point to a significant increase in the company's EPS, according to consensus estimates.

    AMD EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    What's more, AMD's long-term EPS growth estimates have moved up impressively this year.

    AMD EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts.

    Assuming the organization clocks even 30% EPS growth in the three years after 2028, its EPS could reach $56.24 after five years.

    Industry observers note that the Nasdaq Composite index has an average price-to-earnings ratio of 39. Assuming AMD trades at 30 times earnings after five years, in line with its five-year average earnings multiple, its stock price could reach $1,687. That's just over 3.3x AMD's current stock price, suggesting that it has the potential to make investors significantly richer over the next five years.

    Breaking: 5 Student Loan Scams to Avoid in 2026

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that student loan scams can be costly, but they usually leave clues.
    • Sources indicate that the communication might seem realistic, but unexpected fees, unknown contacts and massive promises are usually red flags.
    • Here’s a breakdown of common student loan scams and what to do about them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that student loan scams can be costly, but they usually leave clues. Scammers will often try to hook victims with tempting claims of “act now or miss out” and “we promise to get you student aid.".

    Sources indicate that the communication might seem realistic, but unexpected fees, unknown contacts and massive promises are usually red flags. The age-old adage is true: if an offer sounds too good to be true, it probably is.

    Here’s a breakdown of common student loan scams and what to do about them.

    » MORE: How to spot student loan repayment scams.

    The scam: A fraudulent private firm offers to manage your student loans and help you get them relieved or even fully forgiven. These services can cost more than $1,000, and there’s no guarantee that you’ll actually get the help you’re looking for.

    It has been revealed that how to avoid it: You can manage your federal student loans for free. According to the U.S. Department of Education, you never have to pay for help with your federal student loans[1]U.S. Department of Education. Avoiding Student Aid Scams. View all sources . You can work with your loan servicer to adjust your payment plan, consolidate loans and apply for loan forgiveness at no cost to you.

    If you’re being promised immediate student loan forgiveness, are asked for personal identification information like your FAFSA login credentials or asked to authorize a power of attorney, proceed with caution — it’s likely a scam.

    » MORE: How to get help with student loans.

    Recent findings suggest that the scam: A company charges you an upfront fee to combine multiple student loans into one new loan to reduce your monthly payment. The company may be illegitimate and is likely to pocket the fee without actually consolidating your loans.

    How to avoid it: You can consolidate federal student loans for free. There is no fee to consolidate your loans through the Department of Education at studentaid.gov. If you’re looking to reduce your monthly payment through consolidation, start by contacting your loan servicer. And if you get unsolicited communication from a tech giant promising federal student loan consolidation, it's probably a scam.

    According to recent reports, the scam: Scammers use transitions in federal loan programs to take advantage of borrowers. For example, the Education Department was set to resume wage garnishments after a long pause, but in January 2026 unveiled a temporary delay implement repayment reforms.

    According to recent reports, when federal decisions go back and forth like this, it creates a gray area for scammers to make wage garnishment threats. For borrowers who may not know if wage garnishment restarted, it can be hard to know what to do. This goes for other federal changes, too; any uncertainty can be an opportunity for bad actors to take advantage of the confusion.

    How to avoid it: If your wages are truly being garnished, the communication will come from the federal government and not a private company. Likewise, if a company offers to stop your wage garnishment for a fee, you’re probably getting scammed.

    In a recent development, the scam: Criminals impersonate a real person and apply to colleges in their name. Then, they can collect financial aid, take out loans and use their college admission to net discounts on goods and services. This is known as a “ghost student” scam.

    How to avoid it: Follow the steps on identitytheft.gov to report fraud and get a recovery blueprint. There are a few safeguards you can put in place to prevent this form of identity theft, such as setting up a credit freeze and monitoring your FSA ID activity.

    How it works: You might receive a call from someone claiming to be from your school’s financial aid office saying you have unpaid tuition. The caller may threaten that you cannot start your classes until your tuition bill is paid in full. Scammers can be creative and convincing, even going so far as to replicate a school’s phone number to display on your caller ID.

    According to recent reports, how to avoid it: The Federal Trade Commission warns that schools will not call and pressure you to pay tuition[2]Federal Trade Commission. Got a call about unpaid college tuition? It could be a scam. Accessed Nov 16, 2026. View all sources . Rather than trust the caller, use your school's secure student portal to check your account balance. Know for certain what you owe and to whom before sending money. You can also call your financial aid office to confirm the legitimacy of a phone number that has called you requesting tuition funds.

    Realizing you’ve been scammed is stressful, and it’s natural to feel overwhelmed or embarrassed. But acting quickly can make a real difference. The sooner you report what happened, the better your chances of limiting the financial damage and getting your accounts back on track. Here’s what to do:.

    Sources indicate that if you’ve already paid a scammer, report the problem to the bank that issued the payment. If you paid with a credit card, for instance, contact the company and tell them what happened. They may be able to freeze your account or reverse the transaction.

    Reach out to your federal student loan servicer as well and report what happened. They can check to make sure no changes have been made to your account and, in the case that changes did occur, they can help you get your loan back on track.

    In a recent development, file complaints with the Education Department, the Federal Trade Commission and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. Filing complaints with these agencies helps hold scammers accountable, can result in enforcement action or business shutdowns, and in some cases may help you recover lost funds.

    » MORE: How to recover from a scam.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    A Familiar Setup for Crypto? November 2026 Is Starting to Look a Lot Like November 2022.

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, sorry to say it, cryptocurrency investors, but crypto's slump into November 2026 looks an awful lot like the crypto winter of November 2022, even though the market got a reprieve in the late summer and early fall.
    • So did the crypto bear market really end this summer, or was the excitement just a particularly vigorous bear-market rally that ended up spawning a lot of latest, worthless projects?
    • The summer rally looked so convincing at the time that it seemed to portend an exciting newly introduced crypto bull market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, sorry to say it, cryptocurrency investors, but crypto's slump into November 2026 looks an awful lot like the crypto winter of November 2022, even though the market got a reprieve in the late summer and early fall. In that last crypto winter in 2022, Bitcoin (BTC +0.07%) fell 77% from its peak, which came right after the FTX crypto exchange collapsed.

    So did the crypto bear market really end this summer, or was the excitement just a particularly vigorous bear-market rally that ended up spawning a lot of latest, worthless projects? Let's dig into the historical data a bit more and make a determination.

    The summer rally looked so convincing at the time that it seemed to portend an exciting newly introduced crypto bull market.

    Sources indicate that bitcoin gained about 44% in the third quarter and hit $87,395 in the week ended Sept. 27. As of Nov. 16, it has fallen 23% without pausing much along the way, pushing it past the 20% decline that constitutes a bear market. Other leading cryptoassets, like Ethereum (ETH -1.35%), Solana (SOL +3.52%), and Zcash (ZEC +8.88%), have also performed quite badly since then:.

    The sharp decline of Zcash is particularly troublesome, as it was one of the very few coins that managed to rally during the past 12 months as everything else was falling. It's also one of the assets that many investors, including yours truly, had considered a prime candidate to lead a newly introduced bull market, similar to Solana's role in the early phases of the 2023 bull market.

    Here, two other echoes of 2022 are so loud that they're hard to ignore.

    On Oct. 29, hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance, the largest crypto exchange. In 2022, FTX's collapse delivered the final leg down, pushing Bitcoin to $15,480 by Nov. 22.

    Industry observers note that then, on Nov. 10 of this year, October's Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 0.4% versus the 0.3% expected, and now the market is largely anticipating a Federal Reserve interest rate hike at its next meeting. In November 2022, the Fed raised its benchmark rate range to 3.75%-4%, marking its sixth increase that year. This year, it raised rates to that same range on Sept. 16, then held there on Oct. 28, with two Fed officials dissenting in favor of another increase. Such hiking cycles tend to be toxic for riskier assets like crypto.

    This time around, a few of the other details are slightly different.

    Binance states it will be able to cover its users' losses from the hack, whereas FTX went bankrupt, and its customers waited more than two years for repayments that began in February 2025. In 2022, the degree of connection between the traditional financial sector and the crypto sector was much weaker.

    Today, spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) exist, and they let capital flow from one sector to the other much more freely than before, which could attenuate the intensity of a drawdown -- or perhaps make it worse.

    Measured from its September high, Bitcoin is already back in a bear market, so the real question is whether its July 1 low of $57,749 will hold. It's still above that level as of Nov. 16, and I doubt it will break below that, but it's possible.

    The more important point here is that if you're an investor with a long-term outlook, as you probably should be, a continuation of the bear market would be an opportunity to look for bargains rather than a cause for despair.

    According to recent reports, the next recovery could also have a bigger tailwind than before. In June 2026, Citigroup projected that the base of tokenized assets (stocks, bonds, and funds recorded as blockchain tokens) would grow from about $17 billion to reach a value in the ballpark of $5.5 trillion by 2030 in its base case. That money won't lift every coin, though. Bitcoin benefits most directly, as institutions compete for a fixed supply, while Ethereum's and Solana's networks earn fees only when that activity settles on their public chains.

    According to recent reports, smaller coins look even riskier than usual given the current backdrop of uncertainty. CoinGecko research in 2025 found that 53.2% of all the cryptocurrencies ever listed on its tracker had failed. Yes, Solana was a small, relatively unknown coin at the start of 2023. But for each Solana, many thousands of tokens went to zero.

    Regardless of what happens next with the price of these coins, it's worth accumulating Bitcoin gradually, and if you're a bit more risk-tolerant than the average crypto investor, consider also accumulating Ethereum, Solana, and Zcash as much smaller slices of a diversified portfolio. I suggest avoiding anything outside the top 15 by market value until market conditions improve.

    That’s why the Rule Breakers approach begins with behavior. This week, two of the six habits deserve extra attention.

    Invest. For At Least Three Years.

    It has been revealed that picture two investors who bought Garmin (GRMN -0.40%) on March 17, 2022. That’s the day Team Rule Breakers recommended it in Stock Advisor, at $111.93. Within months, sales started slipping. The stock fell to the low $80s. It didn’t climb back above $111.93 until late 2023. The first investor gave up during the slump and sold. The second gave the business time. Today, the shares trade around $283. The second investor’s patience paid off.

    Sitting through the slump was only half the job. By late 2024, Garmin had roughly doubled from its recommendation price. That’s when many investors sell half to “play with the house’s money.” Anyone who cashed out at the double, around $224, have missed about another 25% since. Massive winners rarely rise in a straight line. Letting one run means sitting through the swings.

    According to recent reports, you can’t control how Nvidia’s report lands or how Anthropic’s shares trade on day one. But you can choose how you respond.

    #15979. Survey: Gen Z Loves a Winter Challenge, but Money Goals Often Fizzle

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2274 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    Survey: Gen Z Loves a Winter Challenge, but Money Goals Often Fizzle

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that it’s not technically winter yet, but depending on where you live, it may feel like it.
    • “Winter arc” is a popular social media challenge through which people aim to improve themselves before the fresh year.
    • Whether they call it a winter arc or not, plenty of Americans are working on self-improvement as the chill sets in.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that it’s not technically winter yet, but depending on where you live, it may feel like it. For many of us, this is a time of hibernation, but for others, it’s prime time for a glow-up.

    “Winter arc” is a popular social media challenge through which people aim to improve themselves before the fresh year. It typically runs from October through December, but can be started any time during the cold months. The aim is to jump-start the “new year, new me” season before the ball even drops.

    Whether they call it a winter arc or not, plenty of Americans are working on self-improvement as the chill sets in. According to a newly introduced NerdWallet survey, conducted online by The Harris Poll, 75% of Americans say they’re working on their physical health, and 69% say the same about their finances.

    Popular as it is, winter arc isn’t the only cold-weather challenge out there. The survey found that half of Americans (50%) say they’ve tried some sort of winter improvement challenge. And no one likes a challenge like Gen Z: Nearly three-quarters of Gen Zers (74%) have tried a winter challenge, compared with 64% of millennials, 42% of Gen Xers and 29% of baby boomers.

    Note: The survey defines Gen Zers as those 18-29; millennials, ages 30-45; Gen Xers, ages 46-61 and baby boomers, ages 62-80.

    Industry observers note that but there’s a difference between starting a challenge and successfully completing one. Gen Zers reign supreme as those most likely to hop on a winter challenge. But they’re also the most likely to say they generally quit challenges before finishing, buy products they saw on social media in an effort to stick with the challenges and set the same financial goal more than once.

    Gen Zers are more likely than any other generation to say they:.

    Have tried a winter financial challenge other than no-spend January (21%, vs. 11% of millennials, 5% of Gen Xers and 2% of baby boomers).

    Sources indicate that generally quit challenges before they finish them (59%, vs. 42% of millennials, 36% of Gen Xers and 22% of baby boomers).

    Expect to spend more on at least one discretionary expense this winter than they would during another season (90%, vs. 83% of millennials, 61% of Gen Xers and 48% of baby boomers).

    Put off dealing with money until after the holidays (60%, vs. 47% of millennials, 35% of Gen Xers and 15% of baby boomers).

    Industry observers note that aren’t at the moment working on improving their finances, but want to make it a priority (15%, vs. 8% of millennials and 6% each of Gen Xers and baby boomers).

    According to recent reports, “Embracing the winter arc trend can be a great way to find motivation to make progress on a goal over the slower winter months,” says Kimberly Palmer, personal finance expert at NerdWallet. “Pick a winter challenge that aligns with a longer-term goal for the coming year.”.

    Winter challenges popular with Gen Z include diet- or fitness-related challenges (29%) and self-improvement challenges, like winter arc or 75 Hard, a mental toughness challenge that runs for 75 days and includes two workouts every day, a strict diet and daily nonfiction reading (25%).

    While winter arcs typically focus on physical, mental and intellectual self-improvement, Gen Z is game to try a financial challenge as well: One long-standing financial challenge — no-spend January — is more popular among younger Americans (22% of Gen Zers and 20% of millennials) than their older counterparts (12% of Gen Xers and 6% of baby boomers). As for other types of financial challenges, Gen Z is more likely than any other generation to have tried at least one: 21% compared with 11% of millennials, 5% of Gen X and 2% of baby boomers.

    Of course, it’s one thing to try a challenge, during wintertime or otherwise. It’s another thing entirely to follow through and complete it. That’s the hard part for many Gen Zers.

    When taking on a self-improvement challenge, the beginning tends to be easiest. You’re motivated and excited to reach goals and better yourself. But as time goes on, it’s easy to slip back into old habits or for the shine of a brand-newly introduced challenge to dim. And Gen Zers report that they are most likely to quit early.

    Sources indicate that according to the survey, nearly 3 in 5 Gen Zers (59%) say they generally quit challenges before they finish them. That compares with 42% of millennials, 36% of Gen Xers and 22% of baby boomers.

    Sources indicate that along with challenges in general, money goals can be difficult to follow through with, especially for younger Americans. Around two-thirds of Gen Zers (64%) say it’s been hard to stick to financial goals they’ve set in the past, compared with 52% of Gen Xers and 34% of baby boomers. Gen Zers are more likely than any other generation to say they’ve set the same financial goal more than once because they didn’t stick with it — 33%, compared with 20% of millennials, 15% of Gen Xers and 7% of baby boomers.

    This isn’t for lack of desire, though. Seven in 10 Gen Zers (70%) say they’re working on improving their finances. All generations show high levels of effort here: 76% each of millennials and Gen Xers say the same, along with 59% of baby boomers.

    So why is it so hard to stick with money goals? One possibility is that it’s difficult to see meaningful progress on finances, particularly when you’re young. According to the survey, 65% of Gen Zers say it’s harder to see progress on financial goals than on physical goals.

    According to recent reports, this makes perfect sense for this age group — for those light on money but rich in youthfulness, desired physical changes may show up faster than financial progress. On top of that, the current job market is tough for younger Americans. Recent college grads now have a higher unemployment rate than workers in general. Even if you’re still on the job hunt, your 20s are a great time to start taking steps, however small, toward building future wealth.» MORE: I’m 25. Here’s How I Got Started Investing.

    “To increase your chances of success, try coordinating winter arc looks with a friend or giving yourself smaller goals along the way,” Palmer says. “Leaning on the support or coaching from a loved one can make it easier to keep going, as can celebrating incremental progress.”.

    Self-improvement is a noble pursuit. But as with most things in life, it’s easy to lose sight of the ultimate goal in favor of buying things to help you reach it.

    Industry observers note that “It’s easy to feel like a quick purchase can help us meet our goals, and sometimes a product can be a useful tool, but the reality is that true winter arc progress comes from putting in the hard work. There’s no option for ‘purchasing’ it instead,” Palmer says.

    It has been revealed that according to the survey, more than a quarter of Gen Zers (26%) say they’ve bought a product they saw on social media to help with a personal goal or challenge. This is more than any other generation: 17% of millennials, 11% of Gen Xers and 7% of baby boomers say they’ve made social media buys for self-betterment.

    Sources indicate that some self-improvement purchases may be billed on a monthly basis. More than 1 in 5 Gen Zers (23%) say they're still paying for a subscription or membership they signed up for during a past goal or challenge. This is also true for 17% of millennials, 9% of Gen Xers and 2% of baby boomers.

    Recent findings suggest that these challenge purchases may pile onto already higher winter expenses. A majority of Gen Zers (90%) say they expect to spend more on at least one discretionary expense this winter than they would during another season, more than any other generation. Top expenses include food delivery (38%), entertainment at home (35%) and indoor family entertainment (30%). A quarter of Gen Zers (25%) expect to spend more on fitness or wellness apps this winter compared to other seasons.

    Some may be spending more to make themselves feel better during the cold, gray months. Nearly 1 in 5 Gen Zers (18%) say they tend to combat winter blues by spending money, compared with 10% of Gen Xers and 3% of baby boomers.

    The holiday season is an expensive time of year for many of us, and it’s easy to sweep finances under the rug until the fresh year. According to the survey, 3 in 5 Gen Zers (60%) say they generally put off dealing with money until after the holidays. This is more than any other generation: 47% of millennials, 35% of Gen Xers and 15% of baby boomers say the same.

    Even for those taking on financial challenges before the latest year hits, it’s easy for the resulting “savings” to disappear. Nearly three-quarters of Gen Zers (74%) say money they save by cutting back in one area usually just gets spent somewhere else instead of staying “saved.” This is also true for 68% of millennials, 63% of Gen Xers and 45% of baby boomers.

    According to recent reports, for some, the holidays are just one thing competing for their money. Over half of Gen Zers (52%) say they’d rather spend money on how they look now than save it for their future financial security. This compares with 26% of Gen Xers and 13% of baby boomers.

    We don’t begrudge anyone for their desire to look and feel their best this upcoming season. But that doesn’t have to mean you can’t level up your money at the same time.

    According to recent reports, more than 2 in 5 Gen Zers (43%) say they’re putting consistent work into improving their finances, and 27% are putting some work into this, but not consistently. Moreover, 15% of Gen Zers aren’t working on improving their finances but want to make them a priority. No matter your age, here are some ideas for a financial glow-up before the spring thaw.

    Start small if you tend to quit. Nearly 2 in 5 Americans (38%) say they generally quit challenges before finishing them. Early-challenge motivation can make it easy to overcommit. If you often take on challenges impulsively then peter out a few weeks later, try starting small. For example, maybe no-spend January is a stretch, but you can still save by intentionally creating two no-spend days a week.

    In a recent development, move money the day you save it. Over 3 in 5 Americans (61%) say money they save by cutting back in one area usually gets spent somewhere else. If you’re cutting back, transfer the difference to savings that same day, so it can’t leak out elsewhere.

    According to recent reports, make money progress measurable. Half of Americans (50%) say it’s harder to see progress on financial goals than physical goals. There’s a saying that what gets measured, gets managed. Choose one number to track. This might be down payment savings, debt payoff progress or an investment milestone. It may not move much month to month, but you’d be surprised at the difference a year can make, even without a ton of money each month to dedicate toward your goal.

    In a recent development, begin before January. More than a third of Americans (37%) say they put off dealing with money until after the holidays. Facing your finances during the often busy and expensive final months of the year can be daunting, but don’t put your head in the sand until after the holiday credit card balances come due. Put a cap on your winter spending before the latest year to avoid going overboard during the tempting sales this time of year.

    It has been revealed that “If you’re trying to choose a winter arc, pick one that’s realistic but also a stretch goal, so it’s satisfying to accomplish while not being completely out of reach,” Palmer suggests. “Chances are you’ll be glad with what you got done over the colder months when springtime hits.”.

    #15978. Why a Data Center Slowdown Would Reach Utilities and Electrical Suppliers Before Chipmakers

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (977 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Why a Data Center Slowdown Would Reach Utilities and Electrical Suppliers Before Chipmakers

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that voters across the United States supported restrictions on data center development or rejected proposals favoring latest projects in 40 of 41 local ballot contests on Nov.
    • A slowdown in construction could reduce future infrastructure spending by electric utilities and cut into orders for electrical equipment.
    • It has been revealed that however, chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA -0.63%) could continue selling chips to existing data centers and newly introduced projects in other locations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that voters across the United States supported restrictions on data center development or rejected proposals favoring latest projects in 40 of 41 local ballot contests on Nov. 3, according to Ballotpedia. The results included five full construction bans and three six-month moratoriums, raising the likelihood that some planned data centers will be delayed or canceled.

    A slowdown in construction could reduce future infrastructure spending by electric utilities and cut into orders for electrical equipment.

    It has been revealed that however, chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA -0.63%) could continue selling chips to existing data centers and newly introduced projects in other locations. Hence, the earliest signs of a slowdown in the build-out may appear in electricity contracts and equipment orders rather than chip sales.

    Data center developers often request electricity capacity from utilities while their projects are still in the planning stages. However, not all of these requests lead to actual construction.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:53 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Developers initially requested more than 30,000 megawatts of electricity capacity from American Electric Power's (AEP -0.49%) Ohio subsidiary. After American Electric Power Ohio introduced requirements for paid engineering studies and binding financial commitments, requests totaling 13,023 megawatts proceeded to studies. Developers had signed new contracts for only 5,642 megawatts by February 2026. Another 12,219 megawatts had already been contracted before American Electric Power Ohio's new data center tariff took effect in July 2025.

    According to recent reports, this does not mean actual electricity demand declined. Instead, many developers that initially requested power capacity did not proceed with binding contracts. A similar reduction in fresh commitments could signal slower future construction without immediately affecting electricity sales to existing customers.

    Growing electricity demand from data centers can create newly introduced investment opportunities for utilities. Large projects may require new power plants, substations, and transmission lines, allowing regulated utilities to earn returns on additional infrastructure investments.

    This opportunity is reflected in American Electric Power's expansion plans. The firm expects 84 gigawatts of incremental contracted load by 2031. To support that growing demand, the company plans to invest about $100 billion from 2027 through 2031, primarily in power generation, transmission, and distribution. These investments are expected to increase its rate base, or the value of regulated assets on which it can earn returns, to $162 billion by 2031.

    It has been revealed that however, if some of those planned data centers are delayed or canceled, American Electric Power may need to postpone some of its own infrastructure investments. This could slow its earnings growth, although lower capital spending would also reduce its borrowing needs. Hence, a reduction in upcoming data center projects would affect utilities' future growth opportunities before reducing their current electricity sales.

    Data center construction also drives demand for transformers, switchgear, and other electrical equipment. If newly introduced projects are delayed, suppliers could receive fewer orders while continuing to deliver equipment already booked.

    NYSE · As of 9:49 AM ET 11/17/26.

    According to recent reports, eaton (ETN +1.83%) manufactures electrical equipment used in data centers and other industries. In the third quarter, it reported that orders from data center customers across its electrical businesses more than doubled over the preceding 12 months.

    Recent findings suggest that hence, a slowdown in new orders might not immediately affect Eaton's revenue. However, if orders continue weakening, the company could eventually face slower sales growth and lower factory utilization.

    It has been revealed that at its Nov. 12 closing price, Eaton traded at about 26 times its expected 2026 adjusted earnings. Slower earnings growth could put pressure on this valuation. However, demand from utilities, industrial customers, and aerospace could help offset weakness in its data center business.

    According to recent reports, chipmakers may not face the same immediate impact from delayed data center construction. Their customer will likely continue to buy chips to upgrade existing facilities or install them at other locations with available electricity and cooling capacity.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:52 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Nvidia is scheduled to report its fiscal third-quarter results on Nov. 17. The firm was guiding for total revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, up from $96.2 billion in the second quarter. However, its actual results will provide a more recent indicator of demand for its artificial intelligence (AI) chips.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:49 AM ET 11/17/26.

    Microsoft (MSFT -1.20%) has already demonstrated how chip spending could remain strong despite data center construction delays. In its recently reported quarter, Microsoft's capital expenditures totaled $45.2 billion. Approximately three-quarters of this spending was for shorter-lived assets such as CPUs, GPUs, memory, and storage. This spending continued despite delays in third-party data center capacity.

    Recent findings suggest that however, prolonged construction delays could eventually affect chip demand, as latest servers require sufficient power and cooling capacity. Nvidia had $279 billion in supply and manufacturing capacity commitments at the end of July, although some agreements can be adjusted before becoming firm orders. If customers delay chip purchases due to limited data center capacity, Nvidia could face risks associated with these commitments.

    Hence, Nvidia's upcoming results and management's outlook could help investors assess whether data center construction delays are beginning to affect semiconductor demand.

    Industry News: Mortgage Rates Today, Tuesday, November 17: A Little Higher

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates keep rising as markets anticipate a near-certain Fed rate hike next month.
    • Recent findings suggest that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.34% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates keep rising as markets anticipate a near-certain Fed rate hike next month.

    Recent findings suggest that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.34% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is seven basis points higher than yesterday and 34 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

    According to recent reports, the results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

    Industry observers note that investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

    » MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.84% or higher.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    Industry observers note that » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    Industry observers note that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    Recent findings suggest that nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a newly introduced home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Industry observers note that » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    Investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure organization Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    After hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he said.

    "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," said DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    Recent findings suggest that while Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as fresh contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    Sources indicate that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," stated Gesuale.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space tech giant with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst noted, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    Could This Under-the-Radar, Cash-Rich Stock Be a 10-Bagger By 2030?

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, I won't sugarcoat it.
    • Owners are coming back, the company is close to breaking even, and it has a large cash cushion relative to its size.
    • Recent findings suggest that in the third quarter, Nextdoor's revenue rose 14% year over year, ahead of expectations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, I won't sugarcoat it. Nextdoor (NXDR -1.23%) has been a tough investment to own since it went public in 2021 at $10 per share. The stock is down roughly 80% since then, and for a while it wasn't clear that the neighborhood social network could grow at all, at least profitably.

    That's starting to change. Owners are coming back, the company is close to breaking even, and it has a large cash cushion relative to its size. With a market value of about $790 million, it's fair to ask whether Nextdoor could be a 10-bagger from here. Here's the bull case, and the hurdles.

    Recent findings suggest that in the third quarter, Nextdoor's revenue rose 14% year over year, ahead of expectations. Platform weekly active people also grew by 14% to a record 24.5 million, the third straight quarter of sequential growth. What's more, management noted the growth came mostly from returning users and product improvements, not paid marketing, and the number of people posting each week rose 27%.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:56 AM ET 11/17/26.

    CEO and co-founder Nirav Tolia believes Nextdoor is uniquely positioned to thrive in the AI age. In a world where more of the internet is becoming synthetic, he argues, real people verified to a real place become scarce. That's a compelling angle as AI-generated content floods the rest of social media. But could the stock be a 10-bagger for investors who buy at these levels?

    In the third quarter, Nextdoor's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) more than doubled to $10.3 million, and Nextdoor's net loss shrank to less than $1 million. It's worth noting that GAAP results still benefit from interest income on the more than $380 million in cash on its balance sheet, and that stock-based compensation remains high at 18% of revenue. The former adds to the bottom line, while the stock-based comp is the main reason Nextdoor is yet to achieve GAAP profitability.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking of cash, the balance sheet is a major strength. Nextdoor ended the quarter with $382 million in cash and investments and no debt. That's nearly half of its market value, and the organization has a $100 million buyback program in place to take advantage of weakness in the stock price.

    To be sure, a 10x return from Nextdoor would mean a market value of roughly $8 billion. If the market valued Nextdoor at about 5 times sales, a reasonable valuation for a profitable social platform, that would require roughly $1.6 billion in annual revenue, or a little more than five times this year's expected $294 million.

    Sources indicate that that's where the bull case runs into trouble. Average revenue per user rose just 1% last quarter. Nextdoor's audience is growing faster than its ability to monetize it, and it competes with much larger platforms for local advertising dollars. As a small-cap stock, it can also be volatile. However, the top-line growth has been accelerating, and if the organization can figure out how to improve monetization, a 10x isn't outside the realm of possibilities.

    According to recent reports, in fairness, getting to $1.6 billion in revenue by 2030 might be pushing it, even if things go well. But this is a small manufacturer with tremendous upside potential if management can figure out profitable long-term growth (and the signs since Tolia returned as CEO have been mostly positive). After all, Nextdoor could 10x from its current price and have a smaller market cap than either Snap (SNAP +5.60%) or Pinterest (PINS +0.38%). Plus, keep in mind that if the company gets aggressive with its buyback program at the current level, it could reduce the share count and help drive per-share value.

    Having said all that, Nextdoor is more interesting today than it's been in years. It has a unique asset in 15 years of verified local conversations, its users are growing again, and its cash pile gives it time to figure out monetization. I own Nextdoor and like what I've been seeing in recent quarters, and I think it's just a matter of time before the market starts to appreciate the tech giant's positive momentum.
